items.title: Snooze: read state, toggle it, freeze/unfreeze Stream channels
items.capability: A member can put their profile to sleep (hidden from discovery, chats frozen) and wake it up again from the web app, instead of having to reach for their phone.
sub_items: Doc settings-row 'SNOOZE' / item 44 — toggle switch labelled 'Snooze my profile' with the section title + description copy
Item 48 — read current state on mount via AppSync GET_USER_SNOOZE_STATUS → getUser.isSnooze
Item 49 — toggle posts to USERS_LAMBDA with type 'snooze' / 'noSnooze'
Item 50 — on snooze, freeze EVERY Stream channel the user is a member of, system text FROZE_CHANNEL_COPY ('Currently taking a break')
Item 51 — on unsnooze, unfreeze only channels whose OTHER member is not also snoozed (isSnoozeContactValidationUtil), system text UNFROZE_CHANNEL_COPY
Item 52 — success toasts SET_TO_SNOOZE_SUCCESS / UNSNOOZE_SUCCESS
Cross-screen gap 1 (provider half) — web needs a snooze state holder; mobile wraps the whole authenticated tree in SnoozeProvider
D3 (snooze half) — no SnoozeProvider equivalent mounted in app/(app)/layout.tsx
Cross-screen gap 2 (snooze half) — add 'snooze' / 'noSnooze' to lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts
items.acceptance: (1) Unit: snoozeOrUnsnooze(id,true) invokes raiseUserLambda with payloadType 'snooze' and (id,false) with 'noSnooze' — assert on a mocked lib/aws/raiseUserLambda. (2) Unit on the pure predicate shouldUnfreeze(members, myId, otherIsSnooze): returns false when the other member isSnooze, true otherwise. (3) Playwright: check the toggle in /settings, assert exactly one lambda Invoke whose JSON body.type === 'snooze'; reload the page with a stubbed GET_USER_SNOOZE_STATUS returning isSnooze:true and assert the toggle input has checked===true.
items.evidence: MOBILE has it: src/screens/settings/home/HomeSettings.tsx:24 renders <SnoozeSwitchLayout/>, whose handler is SnoozeProvider.handleTogleSnooze (src/context/snooze/SnoozeProvider.tsx:45-59) calling snoozeOrUnsnooze (src/utils/lambda.ts:188) and updateFrozenChannels (:62-87). WEB does not: `grep -ril snooze` over cancerbuddy-web returns only read-side field usages (lib/buddies/discoveryFetch.ts:204 filters isSnooze:{ne:true}, lib/groups/members.ts:29, components/buddies/BuddyIdSheet.tsx:60) — no write path, no provider, and lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts:6-63 has neither 'snooze' nor 'noSnooze'.

items.evidence: MOBILE gates seven navigators on isSnooze (grep 'SnoozeLayout' src/navigation → BuddiesNavigation.tsx:18, GroupsNavigation.tsx:20, UpdatesNavigation.tsx:18, ProfileNavigation.tsx:19, FeedsNavigation.tsx:19, StreamingNavigation.tsx:16, RequestBuddiesNavigation.tsx:17) and hides header CTAs at HamburgerHeader.tsx:104-127. DOC CORRECTION: the doc summary says the empty state appears 'across chat/groups' — chat is NOT one of the gated navigators; the correct list is the seven above.

items.title: Delete account: reason picker, confirmation, dual-Lambda deletion, success screen
items.capability: A member can permanently delete their CancerBuddy account and all its data from the web app — the mechanism the published privacy and child-safety policies promise.
sub_items: Doc settings-row 'DELETE ACCOUNT' / item 46 — the settings entry point (caret link 'Delete my account' with its section copy)
Item 55 — screen 'Can you say more?' / 'Help us improve by sharing more info. Your feedback is anonymous.'
Item 56 — reason radio group, the five USER_DELETION_REASONS values verbatim
Item 57 — 'Other' reveals a textarea, placeholder 'Type your answer here', hint '(Maximum 1000 characters)', maxLength 1000
Item 58 — DELETE MY ACCOUNT disabled until a reason is chosen, and until the 'Other' text is non-empty
Item 59 — confirmation modal 'Delete my account' with the exact body copy and a single YES, DELETE button

Item 60 — delete every Stream 'messaging' channel the user belongs to, then raiseUserLambda('delete', GETSTREAM_LAMBDA, {cognitoId, name}) AND raiseUserLambda('deleteAccount', USERS_LAMBDA, {userId}) — the doc lists only the first of the two
Item 61 — record the reason with AppSync CREATE_DELETE_REASON ({reason}; 'Other' stores the free text). Do this BEFORE clearing the session, not after (see evidence)
Item 62 — clear session and route to the success screen
Item 63 — success screen: success image, 'Your CancerBuddy account has been deleted.', 'All your info is safely removed…', X and GOT IT both returning to the signed-out stack
Cross-screen gap 2 (delete half) — add 'delete' and 'deleteAccount' to lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts
items.acceptance: Playwright: on /settings/delete-account the submit button has [disabled] until a radio is chosen; choosing 'Other' re-disables it until the textarea is non-empty. Confirming in the modal produces (a) a POST to AppSync whose body contains 'createDeleteReason' with the selected reason string, (b) a Lambda Invoke with body.type === 'delete' targeting NEXT_PUBLIC_GETSTREAM_LAMBDA, (c) a Lambda Invoke with body.type === 'deleteAccount' targeting NEXT_PUBLIC_USERS_LAMBDA, and finally page.url() === origin + '/' with no CognitoIdentityServiceProvider keys left in localStorage. Assert the network calls in that order.
items.evidence: MOBILE: HomeSettings.tsx:43-57 links to SettingsScreens.DeleteAccount; DeleteAccount.tsx:60-90 runs deleteAccount(id,name); utils/lambda.ts:116 and :125 fire TWO lambda verbs (DELETE→GETSTREAM_LAMBDA, DELETEACCOUNT→USERS_LAMBDA). WEB: `grep -ril 'deleteaccount|delete account|delete my account'` over cancerbuddy-web returns nothing; lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts:6-63 declares neither verb. DOC ERROR: doc item 60 names only the GETSTREAM 'delete' call and omits the USERS_LAMBDA 'deleteAccount' call — porting only the first would leave the user row alive. MOBILE BUG not to copy: DeleteAccount.tsx:73-80 calls registerDeletion() AFTER clearUserFromSession(), so the reason mutation runs on a torn-down session, and navigation to the success screen happens even when the lambda returned nothing.

items.title: Change status — the picker and Path A (Patient ↔ Survivor via updateUser)
items.capability: A member whose condition has changed can switch between 'I've been diagnosed' and 'I'm in remission' from the web app, with the same age- and role-dependent options mobile offers.
sub_items: Doc settings-row 'CHANGE STATUS' / item 45 — the settings entry point (caret link 'Change my status' with its section copy)
Step-1 field row — the status radio group; selecting an option immediately commits and routes
Item 64 — option filtering by current type: PATIENT → offer SURVIVOR + CAREGIVER; CAREGIVER → offer PATIENT only; SURVIVOR → offer PATIENT only
Item 65 — under-18 rule: CAREGIVER removed regardless of current type (displayAge(birth) < MAXAGE, MAXAGE = 18); birth re-read from AppSync on mount

Item 76 / Path A section — copy screen (copiesWhenBecomeSurvivor / copiesWhenBecomePatient with the shared 'you can still keep your buddies' subtitle), CHANGE STATUS button, 'Change my status' confirm modal ('Are you sure you want to change your status to {survivor|patient}?' → YES, CHANGE STATUS), AppSync updateUser with {id, userType, inRemissionSince: last-day-of-current-month | null}, then the confirmation panel ('Your status has been updated.' / 'To continue, log back in…' / GOT IT) and forced sign-out
Routing split (change-status-select.tsx:70-80): SURVIVOR from any, or PATIENT when current is SURVIVOR → Path A; everything else → Path B
items.acceptance: (1) Unit test on a pure changeStatusOptionsFor({currentUserType, birth}) covering six cases: PATIENT/adult → ['SURVIVOR','CAREGIVER']; CAREGIVER/adult → ['PATIENT']; SURVIVOR/adult → ['PATIENT']; PATIENT/under-18 → ['SURVIVOR']; SURVIVOR/under-18 → ['PATIENT']; and the CAREGIVER/under-18 case pinned to the decision recorded in the item body. (2) Unit: routeFor(next,current) returns 'A' for (SURVIVOR,*) and (PATIENT,SURVIVOR), 'B' otherwise. (3) Playwright: confirming Path A issues one AppSync POST containing 'updateUser' whose input.userType is the chosen type and whose inRemissionSince is monthYearToStoredDate of the current month (or null when becoming PATIENT), then lands on '/' signed out.
items.evidence: MOBILE: change-status-select.tsx:50-68 builds optionsComplete/optionsUnderAge, :70-80 splits the two paths; ChangeStatusLayout.tsx:34-46 writes UPDATE_USER. WEB: `grep -ril changestatus` over cancerbuddy-web returns NOTHING — no route, component, store or lambda constant. DOC CORRECTION (scoping): the doc implies this is greenfield, but web already owns displayAge (lib/buddies/age.ts:55), the mm/yyyy + last-day-of-month helpers (lib/profile/monthYear.ts) and an updateUser path (lib/profile/personalInfo.ts), so this is composition, not new infrastructure. MOBILE BUGS not to copy: (a) change-status-select.tsx:29-31 has a useEffect with no dependency array, so GET_MAIN_USER_DATA refetches on every render; (b) optionsUnderAge (:59-62) drops only CAREGIVER and the current type, so an under-18 CAREGIVER is offered SURVIVOR, which optionsComplete forbids — pick one rule and state it; (c) ChangeStatusLayout.tsx:32-46 derives the target from useAuth().userType rather than the selected nextUserType and therefore has no CAREGIVER key, working only because the picker never routes a caregiver here.

Item 67 — 'Almost there!' interstitial with the oneonone.gif, 'Please complete your new status information', 'update my information', and the X escape hatch that abandons the flow

Item 68 — progress bar whose denominator changes with the target type: 4 screens becoming CAREGIVER, 2 becoming PATIENT; the navigator also drops Relationship + Birth when the CURRENT user is a CAREGIVER
Item 69 / field 1 — relationship single-select, placeholder 'Relationship to the patient', required, from listRelationships re-ordered by ORDER_RELATIONSHIPS_COPY

Item 70 / field 2 — patientBirth mm/yyyy masked input, maxLength 7, month clamped 01–12, three validation messages (valid month/year, ≤130 years, correct format), '(mm/yyyy)' hint + 'Why do we ask this?' expander
Item 71 / field 3 — diagnosis multi-select autocomplete ('ADD ANOTHER DIAGNOSIS'), required, placeholder varies by target type
Item 72 / field 4 — treatmentStatus single-select, required (hidden for SURVIVOR, unreachable here)
Item 73 / field 5 — treatments multi-select, cleared and disabled when treatmentStatus.label === 'Pre-treatment', plus the cross-field CONTINUE gate (Pre-treatment OR ≥1 treatment)
Item 74 / field 6 — hospitals multi-select autocomplete with its empty-state copy, required, and the MAYBE LATER skip that jumps straight to Confirmation
Diagnosis screen renders with showDisabilities={false} — side effects are deliberately NOT asked in this flow, unlike enrolment

Item 75 — Confirmation screen ('Your current status' / role subtitle / 'Please log back in…' / 'i understand, continue') building {userId, DiagnosisID[], userTreatmentStatusId, TreatmentsID[], HospitalsID[]} (+ userRelationshipId, patientBirth when target is CAREGIVER), wrapped as patientTocaregivers | caregiverTopatients, posted as 'changeStatus' to USERS_LAMBDA; on HTTP 200 sign out + toast 'Thanks, your profile has been updated.'
Cross-screen gap 2 (changeStatus half) — add 'changeStatus' to lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts
items.acceptance: (1) Unit on the pure buildChangeStatusPayload(values, nextUserType): asserts the exact wire keys userId / DiagnosisID[] / userTreatmentStatusId / TreatmentsID[] / HospitalsID[], the CAREGIVER-only userRelationshipId + patientBirth, and the wrapper key patientTocaregivers vs caregiverTopatients. (2) Unit on progressDenominator(nextUserType, currentUserType) → 4 / 2 / 2. (3) Unit on canContinueFromDiagnosis({treatmentStatusLabel, treatmentIds}) → true for 'Pre-treatment' with zero treatments, false for any other status with zero treatments, true otherwise. (4) Playwright: completing the flow issues exactly one Lambda Invoke with body.type === 'changeStatus' whose payload matches the unit snapshot, then lands on '/' with tokens cleared.
items.evidence: MOBILE: the eight screens are wired in src/navigation/app/change-status/change-status-screens.tsx:15-77; the payload and its wrapper are built in change-status-confirmation.tsx:22-48 and posted by src/services/change-type/change-user-type.ts:9-14 as LambdaPayloadType.CHANGE_USER_TYPE='changeStatus' (src/types/utils/lambda.ts:13). WEB: `grep -ril changestatus` returns nothing and lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts:6-63 has no 'changeStatus'. DOC CORRECTION (scoping): every catalogue this flow needs is already fetched on web — fetchRelationships/fetchDiagnoses/fetchTreatments/fetchTreatmentStatuses/fetchHospitals at lib/aws/appsyncPicklistQueries.ts:199-219 — and every field control already exists in the register and profile surfaces (StepDiagnosis.tsx:108-143 already implements the exact 'Pre-treatment' clear-and-disable rule; PatientInfoForm.tsx:96-155 already does relationship + patientBirth mm/yyyy). The build is the flow, its gating and the lambda call, not the fields. Payload key names verified safe: UserDataKey.treatmentStatus='userTreatmentStatusId' and UserDataKey.relationship='userRelationshipId' (src/model/user/user.tsx:105,109), so formik.values.userTreatmentStatusId is populated, not undefined.

items.title: A sign-out-and-return pattern for account-altering flows
items.capability: After deleting an account or changing status, the member lands on a working signed-out screen instead of being stranded in a half-authenticated shell.
sub_items: Cross-screen gap 6 — both change-status paths and account deletion end by signing the user out and asking them to log back in; web has no shared pattern for that today
items.acceptance: Playwright: a shared helper finishSignedOutFlow() is asserted from all three flows — after the terminal action, page.url() === origin + '/', localStorage contains no key matching /^CognitoIdentityServiceProvider/, and navigating back to /groups redirects to '/' rather than rendering the shell.
items.evidence: MOBILE performs the sign-out explicitly in all three terminal screens (change-status-confirmation.tsx:50-58, ChangeStatusConfirmationLayout.tsx:44-66, DeleteAccountSuccess.tsx:24). WEB's only precedent is AccountSheet.handleLogout (components/app-shell/AccountSheet.tsx:62-72: unregisterPushDevice → disconnectStream → signOut → router.replace('/')); nothing else calls it, and none of the three flows exist yet to reuse it. Mobile's own ChangeStatusConfirmationLayout.tsx:47-56 documents why order matters — signOut makes flaky GetStream/GraphQL calls that can hang, so the UI must switch stacks first.

items.title: Support: send the ticket for real, attributed to the signed-in member
items.capability: A member's feedback or safety report actually reaches CancerBuddy, attributed to their account — today the web form fabricates a ticket id and discards the input.
sub_items: Drawer row 'Tech support & suggestions' — route exists and is well built but submits to a mock

Item 27 / cross-screen gap 4 — replace defaultSupportService = mockSupportService with raiseUserLambda('supportemail', USERS_LAMBDA, {subject, text, userId}); the mock has no dev-only guard and no 'not wired up' affordance
Item 24 — reinstate the 'Community Safety' category (mobile's safety-reporting channel, absent from web) and drop the invented 'billing' category — the app has no billing
Item 28 — attribute the ticket to the signed-in userId; web currently only collects a typed email, so an in-app report loses the account link
Item 29 — surface send failures in the form's own error slot, not in the attachment slot
Item 30 — success confirmation should tell the member where the reply goes (mobile shows the masked Cognito email) rather than only a fabricated ticket id
Decide the fate of web's optional image attachment when the real lambda is wired — mobile has no attachment field, so it either needs a transport or should be removed
Cross-screen gap 2 (supportemail half) — add 'supportemail' to lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts
items.acceptance: (1) Compile/unit: assert `defaultSupportService !== mockSupportService` and that SUPPORT_CATEGORIES includes a community-safety member and excludes 'billing' — a plain unit import assertion, no DOM. (2) Unit: submitTicket({subject,message,category}) invokes a mocked raiseUserLambda with payloadType 'supportemail' and a body of exactly {subject, text, userId}. (3) Playwright: submitting the form from inside the app shell produces one Lambda Invoke whose body.type === 'supportemail' and whose body.userId equals the session's sub claim; forcing that Invoke to reject renders the error inside [data-testid="support-submit-error"] and NOT inside the attachment slot.
items.evidence: MOBILE posts for real: Comments.tsx:38-46 calls raiseUserLambda(LambdaPayloadType.COMMENTS='supportemail', USERS_LAMBDA, {subject, text, userId:id}); the five subject options are SubjectTemplate.tsx:43-52 and include 'Community Safety'. WEB: lib/support/service.ts:9 is literally `export const defaultSupportService: SupportService = mockSupportService`, and lib/support/mockService.ts:13-24 resolves a random CB-XXXX-XXXX after a 600 ms setTimeout without touching the input. lib/support/types.ts:3-10 lists account/billing/content/bug/feature/other — no safety category, and 'billing' has no counterpart in the product. SupportForm.tsx:181 routes submit failures into setAttachmentError.

items.title: Maintenance / app-status gate
items.capability: A member is told the service is in maintenance instead of being shown screens that silently fail.
sub_items: D2 — mobile reads getMaintenanceStatus and reacts to it; web has no equivalent. The optional/required-UPDATE half of that mechanism is not portable (a web app is always the latest build), so only the INMAINTENANCE branch should be built
items.acceptance: Playwright with the AppSync getMaintenanceStatus response stubbed: type 'INMAINTENANCE' makes /groups render [data-testid="maintenance"] and render no app-shell nav; type null renders the normal shell. Unit on the pure statusGateFor(type) → 'block' for INMAINTENANCE, 'pass' for everything else including OPCIONAL_UPDATE and REQUIRED_UPDATE.
items.evidence: MOBILE gates the whole app: Main.tsx:43-50 routes to the StatusApp screen when type === 'INMAINTENANCE' (or REQUIRED_UPDATE), driven by the getMaintenanceStatus query at src/graphql/queries/status-app.ts:3-10. WEB: app/(app)/layout.tsx:20-32 mounts AuthGuard → StreamChatProvider → PushBridge → AppShell and consults no app-status source; grep for getMaintenanceStatus over cancerbuddy-web returns nothing. Scope note: the doc filed this under the drawer because DrawerMenu.tsx:38-49 triggers the optional-update modal on mount, but the maintenance branch is genuinely app-wide and overlaps docs/parity/00-navigation-map.md.

demotions.why: Doc drawer row 'Learn about BMCF' plus items 1, 2 and 3. Same destination, different container: mobile opens https://bonemarrow.org/ in an in-app react-native-webview (src/screens/drawer/website/website.tsx), web opens the identical URL in a new tab (lib/navigation/appNav.tsx:49 BMCF_URL, rendered as an external anchor at :95-100). Items 2 (loading spinner) and 3 (close button restoring the drawer) are artefacts of owning the browser chrome, which a web app does not. The doc itself concedes 'nothing material'.

Doc drawer row 'Read privacy policy, child safety and terms of use'. Web ships the same three documents at app/(legal)/{privacy,child-safety,terms} with content in lib/legal/content.ts; the account-sheet row points at /privacy (lib/navigation/appNav.tsx:120).

Doc drawer row 'Log out'. Items 7, 17 and 10. Items 19 and 22. Item 19 is a mobile full screen with a title and body line, rendered on web as a sheet action — explicitly not a gap. Item 22 is a loader while the link is fetched. Items 23, 25 and 26. Mobile splits subject and comment across two templates with a back arrow; web merges them onto one page with its own copy — pages-to-single-view restructuring. The character thresholds differ in web's favour in every direction: mobile requires ≥20 chars to submit and caps at 1000, web requires ≥10 and caps at 2000; mobile reveals a free-text subject only for 'Other', web always offers one (max 80 vs mobile's 100). No capability is withheld. The genuine losses in this screen — the missing safety category, the mock submit, the lost userId attribution, the error placement and the follow-up-email confirmation — are carried in support-real-submission.

Item 31. Mobile resets the form on focus (useFocusEffect in Comments.tsx:26-30); web's startOver() at app/support/_components/SupportForm.tsx:186-192 resets every field, the attachment and the result behind the 'Send another' action.

Items 37, 38, 39, 40, 41 and 43. lib/legal/content.ts exports PRIVACY_POLICY (:32), CHILD_SAFETY (:151) and TERMS_OF_USE (:233) with the same block hierarchy mobile uses, and components/legal/LegalDocument.tsx:21-55 renders title → subtitle → subtitleAlt → text[] → list[] exactly. The BMCF blurb and logo are in LegalShell.tsx:50,99-103. Item 43's 'Read All' modal is superseded by full-page routes — a container change, not a content loss.

Item 42 and cross-screen gap 7. Web splits one mobile screen into three routes and puts them in the (legal) route group, so following the account-sheet row leaves the app shell. Both are navigation/layout restructuring, and every document remains reachable via the cross-links at the bottom of each page. Worth a 'back to app' affordance as polish, but no capability is missing.

The /settings Notifications card (components/push/PushSettingsCard.tsx) — browser push permission with distinct denied / unsupported / unconfigured states. Mobile handles push at the OS level and has no in-app row. This must survive the settings work: the three mobile sections are additions to this page, not replacements for it.

Covers the web-only additions table rows: /support as a public signed-out-capable route, the CB-XXXX-XXXX ticket id with a copy button, the optional ≤4 MB image attachment, three SEO-titled legal routes with metadata and a related-docs rail, navigator.share, and the /api/contentful/ads proxy that keeps the delivery token server-side. Caveats folded into support-real-submission: the ticket id is currently fabricated by the mock and the attachment currently goes nowhere, so both need a decision when the real lambda is wired — but the public route, the proxy, the legal metadata and the native share sheet should all be preserved.

/become-a-host (a 9-step host application wizard with its own draft storage and Cognito signup service) has no mobile equivalent — hosts are provisioned out of band. /dashboard is a redirect stub to /groups. Neither is touched by any parity work in this document.

notes:
DOC ERRORS FOUND AND CORRECTED (do not re-derive):
1. Item 60 is incomplete. Account deletion fires TWO lambda verbs, not one: raiseUserLambda('delete', GETSTREAM_LAMBDA, {cognitoId, name}) AND raiseUserLambda('deleteAccount', USERS_LAMBDA, {userId}) — cancerbuddyapp/src/utils/lambda.ts:116 and :125. Porting only the GETSTREAM call would leave the user row alive. Cross-screen gap 2's list is therefore five verbs, not the "two" its heading claims: snooze, noSnooze, supportemail, changeStatus, delete, deleteAccount.
2. The doc summary says the snoozed empty state appears "across chat/groups". Chat is NOT one of the gated surfaces. SnoozeLayout is rendered by exactly seven navigators: Buddies, Groups, Updates, Profile, Feeds, Streaming, RequestBuddies.
3. The doc frames change-status as greenfield ("6 form fields" to build). It is not. Web already owns every catalogue (lib/aws/appsyncPicklistQueries.ts:199-219 — relationships, diagnoses, treatments, treatment statuses, hospitals), every field control (app/register/_components/StepDiagnosis.tsx, StepCGRelationship.tsx, StepCGPatientAge.tsx, StepMedicalCenter.tsx; components/profile/MedicalInfoForm.tsx, PatientInfoForm.tsx), the mm/yyyy + last-day-of-month helpers (lib/profile/monthYear.ts) and displayAge (lib/buddies/age.ts:55). StepDiagnosis.tsx:108-143 already implements the exact "Pre-treatment" clear-and-disable rule. Size the two change-status items as composition, not new form infrastructure.

MOBILE BEHAVIOUR TO FIX RATHER THAN COPY (each is recorded on the owning item, repeated here so the merge step sees them):
- change-status-select.tsx:29-31 — useEffect with no dependency array refetches GET_MAIN_USER_DATA on every render. Fetch once.
- change-status-select.tsx:50-68 — the under-18 filter and the by-role filter disagree for an under-18 CAREGIVER (under-18 path offers SURVIVOR, the role path forbids it). Pick one rule; the by-role rule is the intended one, so an under-18 CAREGIVER should be offered PATIENT only.
- ChangeStatusLayout.tsx:32-46 — the Path A target is derived from useAuth().userType instead of the selected nextUserType, so inputOptions has no CAREGIVER key. Derive from the selection on web.
- DeleteAccount.tsx:73-80 — CREATE_DELETE_REASON runs AFTER clearUserFromSession(), and the success screen is reached even when the lambda returned nothing. Record the reason first, and only navigate on success.

ORDERING / DEPENDENCIES:
- lambda-verbs is a one-line prerequisite shared by four items (snooze-toggle-and-backend, delete-account, change-status-path-b, support-real-submission). It is deliberately NOT a standalone item — it is not a user capability — but it is listed as a sub_item on each consumer. Whoever goes first adds the constants to lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts.
- forced-signout-return is a prerequisite for delete-account, change-status-select-and-path-a and change-status-path-b. Build it with whichever lands first.
- change-status-select-and-path-a must precede change-status-path-b: the picker screen and its option-filtering live in the former, and Path B is only reachable through it.
- snooze-toggle-and-backend must precede snooze-app-wide-state (the latter consumes the state the former establishes).
- partners-list unblocks the AdScreen primary-button revert recorded at components/buddies/AdScreen.tsx:12-15.

OVERLAPS WITH OTHER DOCS:
- app-status-maintenance-gate is app-wide (cancerbuddyapp/src/navigation/main/Main.tsx:43-58), not drawer-scoped. It very likely also appears in docs/parity/00-navigation-map.md — dedupe there and keep one copy.
- snooze-app-wide-state touches Buddies, Groups, Updates, Profile and Live surfaces, all owned by other parity docs. It is filed here because the toggle and the state source are here, but the per-screen gating will collide with those docs' items — merge into one owner.
- The doc notes the Languages row was already flagged missing in docs/parity/00-navigation-map.md:146; it lives in the Profile stack and is out of scope for this document, so it is neither an item nor a demotion here.

UNRESOLVED QUESTION FOR THE PRODUCT OWNER (blocks nothing, but the acceptance test needs an answer): the under-18 CAREGIVER option set — see the mobile inconsistency above. The change-status-select-and-path-a acceptance check pins that case to "the decision recorded in the item body", which must be filled in before that test can be written.

notes:
Verification found errors in the doc in both directions; three are worth the merge step's attention because they remove work rather than adding it.

(1) The doc's Medical #6a describes the treatments rule as \"required once a status is chosen\". The source says otherwise: useMedicalInformation.ts:191-221 has two identical branches, so treatments are required unconditionally — including for SURVIVOR, who has no status field, and for CAREGIVER, whose schema does not require one. Classified MOBILE_BUG_DONT_PORT.

(2) Personal #11 (\"the State field disappears entirely — the user cannot see which state they are in\") is wrong. Web's city options are labelled \"{cityName}, {stateAbbreviation}\", so the state is on screen; mobile just splits it across two controls.

(3) Buddy ID #15 and Cross-screen #8 invert the direction. Mobile *refuses* a self-lookup and bounces you to the hub, so a mobile user cannot preview their own public profile; web opens /buddies/<own id> with isSelf suppressing the connect bar. Web is ahead. Likewise Buddy ID #18/#19 (already-buddies, invite-pending) reach the same end state on web via BuddyProfileScreen's connected/pending branches — only the toast is missing.

Ordering constraints. profile-buddy-id-lookup-safety depends on the age-rules helper already in lib/buddies/age.ts and should be built as \"lift BuddyIdSheet's checks into a shared hook, then consume from both surfaces\" — do it before profile-qr-scanning so the scanner feeds the same ladder. profile-medical-help-flow only needs a new view + subject on the existing components/auth/HelpDialog.tsx; it should not spawn a second help component. profile-avatar-crop is pure reuse of components/auth/PhotoCropper.tsx and should land before any other media-upload work touches the avatar path. profile-unsaved-changes-guard is the only item touching four files at once and is the natural candidate for a shared hook; it is also the largest single item here.

Overlaps with other docs. profile-share-the-app belongs to the drawer/settings surface (the mobile element is used by the drawer Share screen, not the profile stack) — expect a duplicate in the app-shell or settings parity doc and merge there if one exists. profile-buddy-id-lookup-safety and profile-qr-scanning overlap the buddies doc, which owns components/buddies/BuddyIdSheet.tsx. Section 14 rows are audited in full in the buddies doc and are recorded here only for completeness. The connect-flow button bar, blocked-user check and connection toasts are explicitly out of scope for this document.

Open question for the product owner: PersonalInfoForm shows the college questions to caregivers, which mobile's CollegesLayout deliberately hides. That is web offering more, not less, so it is not parity work — but it writes CurrentlyInCollege/userCollegeId onto caregiver records that mobile would never produce. Someone should rule on whether to hide it.

Cross-screen #6 (server-side autocomplete became client-side filtering over a 1000-row preload for diagnoses, hospitals and side effects) is demoted as presentation because the capability is identical today, but it is a genuine scaling ticket the moment any of those catalogues passes 1000 rows — worth carrying as tech debt rather than parity.

items.title: Register the browser's FCM token with the backend push pipeline (UserDeviceToken + login/logout Lambda + rotation)
items.capability: A web user can receive push notifications for anything other than a chat message — a buddy request, a buddy acceptance, a new post in their group, a new group member, a live session starting — and stops receiving them on the right device after logging out.
sub_items: Push reg #4: write the FCM token to the AppSync `UserDeviceToken` table (mobile `createOrUpdateFCMToken`), including the cross-account dedupe: find rows holding this token under any other user and delete them before creating ours

Push reg #5: send the token to `USERS_LAMBDA` with the `login` payload (mobile `LoginInLambdaUtil`); web currently sends `token: undefined`. The web equivalent must fire when permission is granted, not at signup, since no token exists at signup time
Push reg #6: call `USERS_LAMBDA` with the `logout` payload carrying the token on sign-out (mobile `logOutAccountLambda`); web has no logout Lambda call at all
Push reg #8: delete the `UserDeviceToken` row on logout (mobile `deleteCurrentFCMTokenOnSessionClose`)
Push reg #3: re-register on token rotation — subscribe to `onTokenRefresh` and repeat both the Stream `addDevice` and the table write; web only re-registers on page load
Push 'what reaches a browser' #54: every notification type in the matrix except MESSAGE exists in the in-app Updates list on web but can never arrive as a browser notification
Cross-screen gap 1 (web is invisible to the backend push pipeline)
Cross-screen gap 6 (token rotation mid-session goes unhandled)
web_refs: lib/push/pushClient.ts:380-429 (registerPushDevice — mints the token, calls Stream addDevice, never writes it anywhere else)
lib/push/pushClient.ts:316-326 (syncPushDevice — the only re-registration path, load-time only)
components/app-shell/AccountSheet.tsx:62-71 (logout: unregisterPushDevice + disconnectStream + signOut, no Lambda, no row deletion)
items.acceptance: Node integration script against the real AppSync endpoint, runnable in CI: (1) after a Playwright run that grants notification permission and enables push, query `listUserDeviceTokens(filter:{userID:{eq:$id}})` and assert exactly one row whose `token` equals the token the browser logged; (2) seed a row holding the same token under a second userID, re-run registration, assert the foreign row is gone and ours is the only one; (3) drive logout in the same Playwright session and assert the query returns zero rows. Plus a pure unit test on the dedupe reducer (given N foreign rows → N delete inputs, then one create) so the branching is covered without the network.
items.evidence: MOBILE writes the row: cancerbuddyapp/src/context/auth/useAuth.ts:80-145 issues FIND_EXISTENT_TOKEN_IN_ANOTHER_ACCOUNTS → DELETE_USER_DEVICE_TOKEN → CREATE_USER_DEVICE_TOKEN, called from StreamProvider.tsx:125-126 alongside client.addDevice. WEB does not: `grep -rn "UserDeviceToken|DeviceToken|onTokenRefresh" cancerbuddy-web` returns zero matches across app/, lib/, components/, public/. lib/push/pushClient.ts:380-429 is the complete registration path and stops at Stream's addDevice. docs/PUSH.md §Divergences 1 confirms `token: undefined` is still sent to USERS_LAMBDA. docs/PUSH.md §'Enabling an event type' confirms only `message.new` is enabled on the Stream side, so Stream cannot substitute for this table.

items.title: Route every push payload shape to its real destination, from one shared function
items.capability: Tapping a push notification takes the web user to the thing the notification is about — the post, the group feed, the buddy requests, the new buddy, the live room — instead of dumping every non-chat notification on the group list.
sub_items: Push routing #42: legacy `data.channel` (a JSON blob carrying `id`) must resolve to `/chat/{id}`; web reads only `channel_type`/`channel_id` and drops it on /groups

Confirmed: TabsNavigator.tsx:31-33 filters on `TabsNav.HomeNotifications`, but TabsScreens.tsx:23-26 registers the stack under `TabsNav.Updates`, and the enum (src/types/navigation/tabs.ts) defines both members with different string values — so the filter never matches and mobile shows Updates to SUPPORT accounts. Do not copy the intent blind. Correct behaviour for web is a product decision, made deliberately: SUPPORT accounts do receive notifications, so showing the tab (as web does today, primaryNavFor only strips /profile) is defensible — but record the choice.
Nav-chrome row 6. totalUnread from useStreamChat feeds the chat badge (components/app-shell/AppShell.tsx:24,38), equivalent to client.getUnreadCount at tab-bar.tsx:90-106.

Push registration rows 1, 2, 7, 10. Token minted via getToken with vapidKey + our own SW registration (lib/push/pushClient.ts:388-396); registered with Stream via addDevice including the 4th provider-name argument web needs because it runs on its own Firebase project (:419-424, docs/PUSH.md); removed from Stream on logout (:334-344, called at AccountSheet.tsx:68); degrades safely when unconfigured (lib/push/config.ts:66-77).

Push registration row 9. Mobile has no in-app push switch at all; web has `cb.push.optOut` plus the Settings card (components/push/PushSettingsCard.tsx, lib/push/pushClient.ts:279-308). Addition, keep.

Permissions row 11. The capability — grant notification permission — exists on web; only the moment differs (Settings toggle at PushSettingsCard.tsx:41-49 vs mobile's initPermission on provider mount, push-notification.provider.tsx:219 → src/notifications/config.ts:3-6). Deliberate and documented (docs/PUSH.md §Divergences 2); prompting on load is penalised by browsers.

Permissions row 12. Mobile re-requests on DENIED (useLocalNotifications.ts:14-20). A page cannot re-prompt once blocked — that is a browser rule, not an omission — and web delivers the same outcome by showing the unblock instructions (PushSettingsCard.tsx:117-121). Capability preserved by a different route.
Permissions row 13. Web has the equivalent copy under `app.push.blocked`, matching mobile's toast at src/utils/requestPermissions.ts:14-18.

Permissions rows 14 and 15. Web observes PermissionStatus.change through useSyncExternalStore (pushClient.ts:180-208) and handles the 'unsupported' platform state with a manifest so iOS PWA installs work (app/manifest.ts). Neither has a mobile counterpart. Keep.

Channels rows 16, 17, 18, 19. Android channel importance/sound (useLocalNotifications.ts:32-38), Android small icon (:49), iOS foreground presentation options and iOS categories (src/notifications/config.ts:8-23) are all platform presentation with no Web Push equivalent, and no actionable categories are defined so nothing is lost. Row 17's separate complaint — that /icons/icon-192.png is the BMCF lockup and is mush at badge size (firebase-messaging-sw.js:35,66-68) — is a design follow-up already recorded in docs/PUSH.md §Limits.
Channels row 20. Mobile stacks repeated pushes from one conversation; web collapses them with `tag` + `renotify` (public/firebase-messaging-sw.js:58-70). Addition, keep.
Channels row 25. `event.notification.close()` at public/firebase-messaging-sw.js:140 is mobile's cancelSingleNotification.

Foreground row 26. Web cannot use firebase `onMessage()` because the worker is hand-written; the worker posts `cancerbuddy:push` to the focused client instead (firebase-messaging-sw.js:113-127) and pushClient.ts:358-376 consumes it. Different mechanism, same capability, documented at pushClient.ts:346-357.

Foreground row 27. Mobile displays an OS notification even in the foreground (useLocalNotifications.ts:40-57); web shows an in-app sonner toast with an Open action (components/push/PushBridge.tsx:53-60). The member is alerted and can act in both. Container, not capability.

Foreground rows 28 and 29. Web skips the alert for the conversation already on screen (PushBridge.tsx:50-52) — mobile always displays — and only a *focused* client is treated as foreground, so a background tab still gets a real OS banner (firebase-messaging-sw.js:113-118). Keep both.

Foreground row 32. `useGroupPost` is never imported: `grep -rn 'useGroupPost' src` in cancerbuddyapp returns only its own definition (src/hooks/useGroupPost.ts:7). The state it writes, `postNotifications`, is only rendered in src/_archive/HomeGroups.tsx:111,118 — an archived file, and commented out there. No mobile user sees a per-group new-post badge. Do not port.

Background rows 35, 36, 37, 40. Web's `push` listener does the display work (firebase-messaging-sw.js:95-137) where mobile's setBackgroundMessageHandler is empty and notifee.onBackgroundEvent carries it; one `notificationclick` handler (:139-169) covers background AND warm-start taps; and de-duplication (mobile's lastProcessedNotifRef) is unnecessary because the browser fires exactly one notificationclick per notification.

Background rows 38 and 39. Mobile needs a pendingNav queue with 1.5s timeouts waiting for auth and navigator readiness (push-notification.provider.tsx:161-169,197-215); web has no such race — the worker focuses or opens a tab at a URL and AuthGuard handles the rest (firebase-messaging-sw.js:144-167), reusing an already-open window rather than a second app instance. Structurally simpler and more reliable. Keep.
Routing row 41. `data.type === 'CHAT_MESSAGE'` with channel_id lands on /chat/{channel_id} (firebase-messaging-sw.js:86-88). The one branch that works today.
Routing row 51. Mobile must call dismissActionSheets()/closeAllModals() on every branch; a web navigation unmounts overlays by construction. Nothing to build.

'What reaches a browser' rows 52 and 53. `message.new` is enabled on the `web` Stream provider and message.updated / reaction.new / notification.reminder_due are off on both platforms (docs/PUSH.md §'Enabling an event type': 'Only message.new is enabled today … which matches what members get on mobile'). The audit summary's point 2 — that this 'independently caps the browser at chat notifications' — is wrong: mobile is capped identically on the Stream side, and its other pushes come from the backend pipeline, which is the real gap (push-backend-token-registration).

'What reaches a browser' row 55. Stream only pushes to a member with no active connection, so an open tab suppresses push to their phone. Pre-existing product behaviour of the Stream integration, present on both platforms, not introduced by web. Documented at docs/PUSH.md §Limits with the fix if it becomes a complaint (disconnectUser after the tab has been hidden). Track as a product decision, not parity work.

notes:
ORDERING. push-backend-token-registration unblocks the most: until the browser's token is in the `UserDeviceToken` table, the only push a web user can receive is a Stream chat message, which makes push-deeplink-routing, push-badge-and-tray-hygiene and the push half of updates-live-refresh untestable end-to-end. Build it first. push-deeplink-routing is still worth doing in parallel (it is pure and unit-testable, and its output — one shared routing function — is what the tray and badge work keys off), but its Playwright acceptance can only run with synthetic notifications until the token work lands.

updates-live-refresh has a dependency choice to make deliberately. Mobile's mechanism is push-driven, so a faithful port waits on push-backend-token-registration. The cheap, honest interim is a refetch on `visibilitychange`, which is independently valuable and covers the reload-a-stale-tab case that mobile does not have. Ship the visibility half now, wire the push half after the token work.

OVERLAPS WITH OTHER PARITY DOCS.
- viewer-snooze-gate is NOT an Updates feature. Mobile gates seven navigation stacks identically (Buddies, Groups, Feeds, Profile, RequestBuddies, Streaming, Updates). Whoever owns the app-shell/profile parity doc should own this item; it appears here only because this doc surfaced it. Do not build it seven times. Related: web has no way for the viewer to *set* snooze either — `grep -rn 'snooze' app components lib` finds no settings toggle and no `snooze`/`noSnooze` Lambda verb in lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts, while mobile has both (LambdaPayloadType.SNOOZE/UNSNOOZE). That belongs to the settings/profile doc, and the gate is useless without it — the gate would only ever trigger for accounts snoozed from the phone.
- requests-shared-interest-line and requests-profile-next-queue both touch `components/buddies/RequestsSection.tsx`, which the /buddies parity doc also owns. Coordinate: RequestCard is shared by both surfaces on purpose (RequestsPanel.tsx:17), so a change lands on both at once — that is desirable, not a conflict.
- push-backend-token-registration adds a `logout` verb to lib/aws/lambdaPayload.ts. Any other doc adding Lambda verbs should merge into the same file in one pass.

TWO DOC ERRORS WORTH RECORDING SO NOBODY RE-OPENS THEM.
1. The 'In remission' badge (§3 row 17) does not render on mobile — `showBadge` defaults to false and ConnectionRequest never passes it. The doc read the prop, not the render.
2. §5 row 4's claim of 'connection-scoped action buttons' on mobile is wrong; the Maybe-later button is gated on `showMaybeLater`, which that navigation path does not pass. Only the Next-queue half of that row is real.
Separately, the audit summary's framing that the Stream `web` provider 'independently caps the browser at chat notifications' is misleading — mobile's Stream provider is capped identically; the asymmetry is entirely the missing UserDeviceToken row.

ONE HYGIENE FIX WITH NO ITEM OF ITS OWN: lib/notifications/fetch.ts:82 asserts the page size matches mobile's. It does not (20 vs 10). Correct the comment and add a row to docs/UPDATES.md §3 — do not change the value to 10. Fold into whichever item touches that file first.

UNRESOLVED. What USERS_LAMBDA does with the `token` field on the login/logout payloads is not visible from either repo — it may itself write or delete the `UserDeviceToken` row, in which case the direct AppSync mutation in push-backend-token-registration would double-write. Read the Lambda source before implementing; the dedupe logic in useAuth.ts:80-129 suggests the client owns the table, but confirm. Also unverified from source: the exact payload shape the backend sends for each non-chat notification type (the routing item's payload table is transcribed from mobile's reader, not from a captured push). Capture one real backend push per type once tokens are registered, and pin the routing unit tests to those captures.

notes: METHOD NOTE — the single biggest correction to the doc: the whole mobile **Groups stack is unreachable**. `src/navigation/groups/GroupsNavigation.tsx` is never imported anywhere (`grep -rn 'GroupsNavigation\|GroupsNavigator' src` returns only its own definition). What ships is the Feeds stack, `src/navigation/app/feeds/FeedsScreens.tsx`. Screens that live under `src/screens/groups/` but are registered in FeedsScreens (EditPost, TwilioVideoRoom, ActiveUsersListGroups, LiveGroupCalendar via a direct import in feeds/home.tsx) ARE live; the rest (feed/Feed.tsx, new-post/NewPost.tsx, post-details/PostDetails.tsx, recommended-groups/*, group-detail/GroupDetail.tsx, join-group/*, host-detail/HostDetail.tsx) are dead. That kills three whole doc sections and one cited mechanism. DOC ERRORS FOUND (in both directions): 1. "PostCard renders every attachment — video and PDF included — as a square " and "posts made from mobile with video or PDF attachments currently render broken". WRONG. Mobile persists `{type,bucket,region,key,mime,...}` with no `url` (utils/feedMedia.ts:41-54); web's `toAttachments` ends with `.filter(a => !!a.url)` (lib/groups/posts.ts:103), so every mobile attachment is dropped before render. Web shows *nothing*, not a broken image. This makes `groups-attachment-normaliser-and-render` a prerequisite for anything media-related, and it needs a presigned-URL resolver, not just markup. 2. "Comment paging past the first page — `latest_reactions_extra.comment.next` → `groupApiGetNetxComments`". That code is in the DEAD Groups-stack thread. The shipping mobile thread reads the whole reaction set from the `newGetReactionsByPost` Lambda with no client cap. The capability gap is still real (web hard-codes `recentReactionsLimit: 25`), but the fix is not "port mobile's paging loop". 3. "`useGroupFeed.removePost` calls `session.userFeed.removeActivity()`" — correct in substance, wrong line reference; it's `posts.ts:327` reached via `useGroupFeed.ts:210`. Also incomplete: comment deletion has the same defect (`deleteReaction` with the caller's reactions token), and mobile routes BOTH own-content and moderated deletes through the same `deleteMessage` Lambda. 4. "Per-reply VIEW N MORE paging, 10 at a time" listed as MISSING. It is client-side slicing of already-fetched `latest_children`; web renders all of them. Web is ahead. Demoted. 5. "Host row → HostDetail ✅ EXISTS" on both sides. Mobile's group-detail host rows have no onPress (GroupDetails.tsx:155-172). Web-only feature. Demoted to WEB_AHEAD. 6. FeedsHome #12/#13 are attributed to `home.tsx`; the NEW badge actually lives in `GroupsList.tsx:79-82,126-131`. Gap confirmed, source corrected. ORDERING CONSTRAINTS for the merge step: - `groups-attachment-normaliser-and-render` must land BEFORE `groups-post-composer-media-attach` and `groups-comment-composer-media` — the shared `FeedMediaAttachment` type and URL resolver are defined there, and until it lands nothing uploaded is visible. - `groups-rich-text-editor` must land BEFORE or WITH `groups-comment-html-and-identity` and `groups-linkify-and-showmore-threshold`: all three touch `lib/groups/sanitizeHtml.ts`, and the editor's output tag set must be reconciled with `ALLOWED_TAGS` in one pass. - `groups-reply-privately` and `groups-ask-the-host` share one find-or-create-DM-channel primitive that does not exist in `lib/chat` yet (only `removeConnection`/`reportConnection`). Build it once. I marked their shared_layer `none` because chat-channel provisioning is not in the supplied layer vocabulary — flag it to whoever owns the Chat/Connections doc, since that audit almost certainly also needs it. - `groups-support-moderation-role` and `groups-delete-via-deletemessage-lambda` both change who can delete what; do the role predicate first so the Lambda work has a correct caller set. - `groups-2000-char-limit` and `groups-rich-text-editor` both change the composer's value model (plain text → HTML); counting characters must count *text*, not markup, so sequence the limit after the editor. OVERLAPS WITH OTHER DOCS: - `groups-new-post-badge` needs a per-group unread store fed by the push worker. `docs/parity/updates-notifications.md` and `docs/PUSH.md` own that plumbing; MEMORY.md notes the `readNotifications` Lambda is broken, which may constrain the design. Coordinate before building. - `groups-author-is-a-link` lands users on `/buddies/[userId]`, whose connect-CTA gating (connection lookup + `isSnooze` + `connectAgeRules`) is the Buddies audit's. Groups only needs the correct href; do not re-derive the gating here. - `groups-analytics-events` needs an analytics module that does not exist anywhere on web (`ls lib/` has no analytics dir). It is cross-cutting for every area doc — the first area to need it should build it, and Groups should not. - The Live/Streaming audit owns `/live/[eventId]`; Groups only links into it and that link is already correct. ONE ITEM THAT IS A GUARD, NOT A CAPABILITY: `groups-host-cannot-leave-own-group`. By the strict definition it is not a GAP — a mobile host does *not* have the leave capability. I classified it GAP anyway because it is a live correctness defect on web (a host can orphan their own group) that would otherwise vanish from the worklist entirely. Reclassify if the product owner prefers a separate "web defect" bucket. UNRESOLVED QUESTION: web's `JoinGroupDialog` computes `needsCode = !group.isPublic && !!group.code` (JoinGroupDialog.tsx:34). A private group with no `code` set therefore joins with one click on web, while mobile blocks it forever (its Join button never enables because `code.length < 6`). Neither behaviour is obviously right. Not carried forward as an item — needs a product decision.

CORRECTIONS TO THE INPUT DOC (each verified against both repos, do not re-open):
1. The Support-channel bootstrap DOES exist on web. `lib/host-signup/bootstrapSupportChannel.ts:123-235` runs the same CREATE_SUPPORT_CONNECTION → createConnection → accept → supportMessage sequence, and both `lib/user-signup/userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:345` and `lib/host-signup/hostEnrollmentFinalize.ts:222` call it during enrollment. The doc's summary bullet and row 37 both overstate the gap; only the *retry* (when the bootstrap threw and `pendingSupportChannel` was set) is missing.
2. The "In remission" badge on mobile's buddy-request card never renders — `ConnectionRequest.tsx:207` passes `badgeText` without `showBadge`, and `AvatarInfoLayout.tsx:78,287` gates the badge on `showBadge` (default false). Do not port it.
3. Rows 24 and 48 are mobile RESTRICTIONS, not web gaps: mobile blocks opening a frozen conversation and disables its overflow menu; web lets you read it (composer locked) and still block/report from it. Classified WEB_AHEAD_PRESERVE — if anyone "fixes" these to match mobile, they are removing capability.
4. Row 140's AsyncStorage `idConnect`/`isRemove` flags have zero readers anywhere in the mobile app. Dead.

ORDERING / DEPENDENCIES:
- `chat-html-message-body` (rich-text) should land before `chat-host-message-cards-render`: the post card renders stored post HTML through the same sanitiser, so building the sanitiser once serves both.
- `chat-host-message-cards-render` should land before `chat-host-message-entrypoints`. Building the entry points first produces messages that render as bare text on web, which is exactly today's failure mode.
- `chat-attachment-send-rich-media` and `chat-attachment-render-video-and-metadata` share the mapper/upload boundary in `lib/chat/useChannelMessages.ts:71-83,220-234`. Do them adjacently or one person will rewrite the other's mapper.
- `connections-liveness-subscriptions` should land before `buddies-withdraw-invite-confirmation` and `buddies-blocked-profile-guard`, since all three touch the same action-bar render predicate on `BuddyProfileScreen.tsx:446-478`. Suggest one shared `showActionBar({isSelf, isSupport, isBlocked, viewerIsHost})` predicate consumed by three items; its unit tests are named in each acceptance field.

OVERLAPS WITH OTHER PARITY DOCS (flag to the merge step):
- `chat-host-message-entrypoints` reaches into Groups: the "Reply to host" affordance lives on the group post fragment and the "Ask to host" one lives in the private-group join modal. If the Groups doc also lists those two, they are the SAME work item — do not schedule twice. The ambassador intro reaches into Profile (mobile triggers it from HomeProfile and from the ambassador badge on a buddy profile); web has no ambassador explainer modal at all today.
- `chat-analytics-events` is the first consumer of an analytics layer that does not exist on web (there is no `lib/analytics`). Every other area doc that mentions `emitEvent` depends on the same foundation — build it once. The signup flows already seed the localStorage gate keys (`userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:91-96`), so the gate semantics are already fixed.
- `chat-phone-capture-gate` needs a phone-capture surface that only exists inside the signup wizard today; if the Settings/Profile doc lists "edit phone number", that is the same component and this item should be scoped to just the gate.
- `buddies-connection-map-indexed-read` changes a query every Buddies surface depends on (discovery subtracts the map). Coordinate with the Buddies-discovery doc.

OPEN QUESTIONS (product, not port):
- Row 148: neither platform can unblock. Worth raising rather than silently preserving.
- Row 96: web accepts .doc/.docx/.txt but mobile renders every `type:'file'` attachment through its PDF viewer. A .docx sent from web will not open on mobile. Either narrow web to PDF or widen mobile's viewer — a decision, not a defect on either side.
- Row 80 (hard vs soft delete): I ranked matching mobile as the fix because mobile is the stated source of truth, but soft delete is arguably the better default. If product prefers soft delete, this item flips to WEB_AHEAD_PRESERVE and mobile changes instead.

"Screens registered in the Buddies stack but owned by other areas" — `FeedDetail` → `/groups/[groupId]`, `PostDetail` → the group feed thread view, `ActiveUsersListGroups` → `/groups/[groupId]/members`, `HomeProfile` → `/profile`, `UserInfoProfileInvite` → `/buddies/[userId]`: all present and owned by the Groups/Profile audits. `ActivitiesFeed` is a Groups-audit question. `SuccessPhoneVerification` is folded into `chat-phone-verification-prompt`; `PartnerNavigator` into `ads-more-resources-cta`.

Traceability for the numbered cross-screen list, all of which restate rows already carried: 1→`buddies-qr-scanner` + `profile-feedback-banner-and-context`; 2→`buddies-ambassador-modal`; 3→`profile-pending-and-maybe-later`; 4→`profile-feedback-banner-and-context`; 5→`profile-gallery-order-and-viewer`; 6→`requests-shared-coincidence-subtitle`; 7→requests row 29 (PRESENTATION, above); 8→`profile-blocked-user-guard`; 9→`chat-phone-verification-prompt`; 10→`chat-support-channel-retry` (main path already present); 11→split between `ads-rows-13-14` (partner links, correct for the platform) and `chat-image-lightbox`/`chat-pdf-experience`; 12→`buddies-revalidate-on-focus`; 13→`chat-video-send-and-play` + `chat-camera-capture` + `chat-image-lightbox` + `chat-pdf-experience` + `chat-upload-pipeline-limits-and-metadata`; 14→`chat-replyhost-asktohost-family`; 15→`chat-touch-reachable-message-actions`; 16→`chat-frozen-channel-enforcement`; 17→`chat-host-flag-from-grouphostid`; 18→`chat-hard-delete-messages`; 19→`chat-send-analytics`; 20→`chat-unread-semantics`.

notes:
DOC ERRORS FOUND (the doc was wrong in both directions — do not re-derive from it):

1. Chat-list row 31 / cross-screen gap 10 assert "a user who signed up expecting a support conversation never gets one on web." FALSE. `lib/user-signup/userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:345` and `lib/host-signup/hostEnrollmentFinalize.ts:222` both call `bootstrapSupportChannelAfterEnrollment` (`lib/host-signup/bootstrapSupportChannel.ts:123`), which runs the same createSupportConnection → createConnection → accept → supportMessage sequence. Only the retry-on-entry is missing. The item was resized accordingly (s, not l).

2. Profile row 30 ("no 'send invite?' confirmation modal on web") is unreachable on mobile: `showConfirmModal` has exactly one occurrence in the entire mobile `src/` tree — the read at `UserInfo.tsx:256`. Nothing sets it. Dead code.

3. Requests row 10's hardcoded "In remission" badge never renders on mobile either — `AvatarInfoLayout.tsx:288` gates it on `showBadge`, which `ConnectionRequest` does not pass. Dead code, not merely a mobile bug.

4. Gallery rows imply mobile can enlarge/browse photos. It cannot — `GalleryScreen.tsx:92-99` is a FlatList of plain `<Image>` with no press handler. The genuine deltas are newest-first ordering (mobile sorts in BOTH `GalleryScreen.tsx:75-77` and `Gallery.tsx:57`; web's `listPictures` query at `lib/buddies/profileDetail.ts:127-133` does not even select `createdAt`) and per-image failure surfacing. Sized down to s.

5. Chat row 102 (push deep link) is marked ⚠️ but the capability is present: `public/firebase-messaging-sw.js:86-87,137-160` handles routing and cold start. Only Stream's legacy `data.channel` JSON-string shape is unparsed — an unverified risk, not a confirmed gap. If a real Stream payload with `data.channel` is ever observed, open a one-line item in the SW's `targetPath()`.

ORDERING / DEPENDENCIES for the merge step:
- `chat-upload-pipeline-limits-and-metadata` must land BEFORE `chat-pdf-experience` (needs `file_size`) and alongside `chat-video-send-and-play` (needs `duration` and a `video` member on `UIAttachment`). Treat the three as one media-upload sequence; `chat-camera-capture` and `chat-image-lightbox` can follow independently.
- `chat-replyhost-asktohost-family` is the single largest item and OVERLAPS THE GROUPS AUDIT. Both mobile entry points live in Groups (`modal-private-group.tsx:90` for AskToHost, `usePostActions.ts:146` for ReplyHost) and web has neither the private-group access-code modal nor the post "reply to host" action. Do not schedule the chat half before the Groups half exists, or there will be nothing that can produce a `type=ReplyHost` navigation. Coordinate with whoever owns the groups doc.
- `chat-send-analytics` requires standing up an analytics layer from zero — web emits nothing anywhere (grep for `emitEvent|gtag|analytics` returns one comment). It is sized m for that reason and will be cheap for every subsequent area, so schedule it early if other audits also want events.
- `profile-feedback-banner-and-context` and `profile-pending-and-maybe-later` both rewrite `BuddyProfileScreen`'s action bar; do them together or back to back, and preserve the web-only Previous button and position indicator (`BuddyProfileScreen.tsx:250-257,487-498`).
- `chat-host-flag-from-grouphostid` changes who can reach the conversation kebab. Land it before or with `chat-frozen-channel-enforcement`, which edits the same header gate at `ChatHeader.tsx:31-32`.
- `ads-more-resources-cta` is BLOCKED on `/partners` shipping (`app/(app)/partners/page.tsx` is a title-only placeholder). Do not schedule it into this programme; attach it to the Partners work.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- `requests-shared-coincidence-subtitle` needs the sender's interests/hospitals/treatments/diagnosis, which `PendingRequest` (`lib/buddies/types.ts`) does not carry. Either widen the pending-requests query or do a per-card fetch as mobile does (`ConnectionRequest.tsx:60-67` fires one `GET_USER_USERS_DATA` per card). The per-card fetch is what makes mobile show `...`; a widened query would make that state unnecessary. Decide before starting — it changes the size from s to m.
- `buddies-qr-scanner` is documented on web as an intentional omission (`components/profile/BuddyIdScreen.tsx:10-12`). It is a genuine GAP by the stated definition, but it is the one item where the existing web code disagrees on purpose. Confirm with the product owner before building rather than after.
- `chat-render-stored-html` needs a sanitizer decision (DOMPurify vs an allowlist renderer). The only realistic producers of `html` bodies are the support/ambassador Lambdas, so confirm what those actually send before choosing.

items.title: Make LIVE detection actually mean "live"
items.capability: A member can tell which of their groups is broadcasting right now, and follow that badge into the session that is actually running.
sub_items: §3 row 1 / cross-screen #1 / lifecycle step 4: LIST_LIVE_GROUPS is missing filter: { inLive: { eq: true } }
§3 row 1 consequence 5: LIST_LIVE_GROUPS is missing the `limit` mobile applies (resultLimit)
§3 row 1 consequence: liveGroupIds selects `inLive` but never tests it, so every returned row counts as live
§3 row 1 consequence 1: every group that ever had a session scheduled wears a permanent LIVE pill in the sidebar and group header
§3 row 1 consequence 2: GroupFeed shows a permanent "Join live" button into a room the token Lambda refuses
§3 row 1 consequence 3: liveEventIdFor is first-wins over an unordered list, so a genuinely-live group can hand out an unrelated event id
§3 row 1 consequence 4 / §2 row 13: LiveCalendar falls back to liveEventIdFor(event.groupId) and inherits the wrong id
§3 row 3 / cross-screen #4: LIVE badges are not scoped to the groups the user has joined
items.acceptance: (1) Pure-function unit test: given rows [{id:'e1',groupId:'a',inLive:true},{id:'e2',groupId:'b',inLive:false}] and joinedGroupIds ['a','b'], the derived live-group set equals new Set(['a']) and liveEventIdFor('b') === null. (2) String assertion on the query constant: LIST_LIVE_GROUPS matches /filter:\s*\{\s*inLive:\s*\{\s*eq:\s*true/ and /limit:/. (3) Playwright with the AppSync POST stubbed to return one inLive:false row: assert page.getByText('LIVE') has count 0 in the sidebar and no anchor with href^='/live/'.
items.evidence: Mobile filters and caps server-side (cancerbuddyapp/src/graphql/queries/live-groups.ts:5 `listLiveStreamingGroups(filter: { inLive: { eq: true } }, limit: ${resultLimit})`) and then narrows to joined groups (src/screens/feeds/home.tsx:83-86 `currenGroupsLive.filter(lg => userGroupIdSet.has(lg.groupId))`). Web's query has neither clause (lib/groups/groupQueries.ts:126-136) and lib/groups/GroupsProvider.tsx:215-218 builds the set from `liveGroups.filter((g) => g.groupId)` with no `inLive` test.

items.title: Give scheduled sessions a route into the room before they are live
items.capability: A host can open their own scheduled session to start it, and a member can walk into a session that has not been flagged live yet — mobile's calendar row does this unconditionally.
sub_items: §2 row 13 / lifecycle step 6: mobile's calendar row navigates into the room for any session; web links to the group unless a session is already running
§5 row 19 / cross-screen #5: /profile/lives shows a LIVE NOW pill and offers no link to /live/{id} — its only navigations are to /profile
Consequence not called out in the doc: because `inLive` is flipped by the first join, a web host currently has no reachable way to start a session at all once the badge query is corrected
items.acceptance: (1) Playwright with the calendar Lambda stubbed to return one upcoming session {id:'e1', inLive:false} in a joined group: assert the row contains an anchor with href '/live/e1'. (2) Playwright on /profile/lives with one session {id:'e1'}: assert an anchor with href '/live/e1' exists. (3) Existing guarantee to keep green: unit test that hasSessionEnded({status:'scheduled', inLive:false}) === false so the room still admits a pre-live join.
items.evidence: Mobile's handleEventPress navigates to TwilioVideoRoom for every row regardless of status (cancerbuddyapp/src/screens/groups/live-group-calendar/LiveGroupCalendar.tsx:166-174). Web gates the room link on liveEventId (components/groups/LiveCalendar.tsx:84-99, computed at :206-216) and ManageLivesScreen renders only a pill (components/profile/ManageLivesScreen.tsx:45-52, no '/live/' string anywhere in the file). The room itself already supports it: lib/live/session.ts:70-82 — "A host joining is what flips that flag, so treating 'not live yet' as unjoinable would lock the host out of starting their own session."

items.title: Calendar must honour active / archived / ended on each session row
items.capability: A host who hides a session stops it being advertised to members, and a member can see that a session already finished instead of reading it as upcoming.
sub_items: §2 row 6 / cross-screen #2 / lifecycle step 3: mobile filters `e.active !== false && !e.archived` before rendering; web filters only id + scheduledAt
§2 row 6: LiveCalendarEvent does not declare `active` or `archived`, so the fields are discarded at the type boundary
§2 row 8 / cross-screen #8 / lifecycle step 10: mobile's StatusBadge renders a grey ENDED pill; web renders LIVE or UPCOMING only
items.acceptance: (1) Pure-function unit test on the calendar visibility predicate: rows [{active:false},{archived:true},{active:true},{}] reduce to the last two. (2) TypeScript compile-time: `active?: boolean | null` and `archived?: boolean | null` added to LiveCalendarEvent — the predicate referencing them fails `tsc --noEmit` if the fields are dropped again. (3) Component/Playwright test: an event with status 'ended' renders a node with the ENDED label and no UPCOMING label.
items.evidence: Mobile drops hidden and archived rows before privacy filtering (cancerbuddyapp/src/screens/groups/live-group-calendar/LiveGroupCalendar.tsx:192-194 `events.filter(e => e.active !== false && !e.archived)`) and has an ENDED branch (:127-133). Web's fetchLiveCalendar filters only `(e) => e?.id && e?.scheduledAt` (lib/groups/liveGroups.ts:45), LiveCalendarEvent at lib/groups/types.ts:73-88 declares neither field, and the badge is a two-way live/UPCOMING ternary (components/groups/LiveCalendar.tsx:52-63). Note the same Lambda row does carry them — lib/profile/manageLives.ts:55-72 selects `archived` and `active`.

items.title: Deep-link a "we're live" push into the room
items.capability: Tapping (or clicking the toast for) a live notification takes the member into that session instead of dumping them on the groups home with no idea which group went live.
sub_items: §4 row 1: extract eventId / groupId / chatChannelId from the push payload
§4 row 2: warm start — a focused tab navigates into the room
§4 row 3: cold start — a click on the OS notification opens the room directly
§4 row 5: de-duplicate repeated handling of the same eventId
cross-screen #3 / lifecycle step 5b: firebase-messaging-sw.js routes every non-`messaging` push to /groups with no read of eventId
§4 bullet: ForegroundPush carries only title/body/path/channelId, so a foreground live push has no event id to route on
§4 bullet: web fires notifyGroupLive itself, so the app produces a notification it cannot act on
items.acceptance: Unit-test an exported pure `targetPath(data)` (extracted from the service worker so it is importable): {type:'LIVE_NOTIFY', eventId:'e1', groupId:'g1'} → '/live/e1'; {type:'LIVE_NOTIFY', groupId:'g1'} (no eventId) → '/groups/g1'; {channel_type:'messaging', channel_id:'c1'} → '/chat/c1' (regression). Plus a React test on the foreground path: dispatch a 'cancerbuddy:push' message with eventId 'e1', click the toast action, assert router.push called with '/live/e1'; dispatch the same eventId twice and assert exactly one navigation.
items.evidence: Mobile reads the payload (cancerbuddyapp/src/context/push-notification/push-notification.provider.tsx:69-81 extractLiveParams), navigates warm (:352-362), resets cold (:45-67 buildLiveDeepLinkState), and de-dupes on `message?.data?.eventId` (:371-377). Web's worker returns '/groups' for anything that is not `channel_type === "messaging"` (public/firebase-messaging-sw.js:85-90) and ForegroundPush has no event field (lib/push/pushClient.ts:55-61, :369-370), while the web room itself sends the push (components/live/LiveRoom.tsx:326-349).

items.title: Restore the scheduling guard rails on the live editor
items.capability: A host cannot schedule a session in the past or more than a year out, picks times on a 15-minute grid, and sees when the session will end before saving.
sub_items: §5 row 11 / cross-screen #7 / lifecycle step 2: date picker minimumDate = now — web's datetime-local input has no `min`
§5 row 12: date picker maximumDate = end of the day one year out — no `max` on web
§5 row 13: time picker in 15-minute steps (minuteInterval={15}) — no `step` on web
§5 row 15: "Ends at HH:MM" live preview, including the cross-midnight "Ends <Mon D> at HH:MM" form — not rendered on web
items.acceptance: (1) Unit test a pure `scheduleBounds(now)` returning {min, max, step}: min === local-ISO of `now`, max === local-ISO of `now + 1 year` at 23:59, step === 900. (2) Unit test a pure `endsAtLabel(scheduledAt, duration)`: same-day → 'Ends at 3:30 PM'; crossing midnight → 'Ends <Mon D> at …'. (3) Playwright/DOM assertion: the datetime input carries matching `min`, `max` and `step="900"` attributes, and the Ends-at text node updates when duration changes.
items.evidence: Mobile defaults min to now and max to +1 year (cancerbuddyapp/src/components/elements/live-schedule-field/LiveScheduleField.tsx:111-112 with buildDefaultMaximumScheduleDate at :56-62), passes minuteInterval={15} to both pickers (:346, :384) and renders endsAtLabel (:174-185). Web's field is a bare input with only value/onChange/className (components/profile/ManageLivesScreen.tsx:391-396) and no ends-at output anywhere in the file.

items.title: Refresh /profile/lives and show a session's real state
items.capability: A host can re-read their session list without leaving the page, sees a session's live state change while the screen is open, edits against fresh server data, and can see when a session was created and last updated.
sub_items: §5 row 16 / cross-screen: pull-to-refresh on mobile's list — web reloads only after a save, so a session going live never updates its pill
§5 row 18: mobile re-fetches the session fresh when the detail opens; web opens the editor from the list row it already has (fetchLiveSession exists and is never called)
§5 row 17: created / last-updated timestamps shown on mobile's detail screen — the fields are already selected on web and never rendered
items.acceptance: (1) Playwright with the AppSync endpoint counted: click the refresh control, assert a second `listLiveStreamingGroups` request is issued and the rendered pill changes when the stub flips inLive to true. (2) Playwright: open a row's editor, assert a `getLiveStreamingGroup` request fires and the form shows the stubbed fresh title, not the stale list title. (3) DOM assertion: with createdAt/updatedAt in the stub, both timestamp strings appear in the editor.
