demotions.why: Every ✅ row in the in-room matrix, §1, §2, §3 and §5 was opened in both repos. The web room calls the same four Lambdas with the same payloads (lib/live/liveService.ts:95-191 vs cancerbuddyapp/src/services/streaming/twilio-video.ts:14-131), wires all four moderation actions (LiveSheets.tsx:230-258), handles received moderation with the same three de-dupes, keeps the screen awake, and derives the same back target. §5 row 6 (no ENDED pill on /profile/lives) is genuinely cosmetic because both platforms filter status==='ended' out of that list before rendering (manageLives.ts:135 vs mobile's client filter).

Verified web-only, and verified absent from the mobile repo rather than merely unrendered: screen share exists only on web (localTracks.ts:132-138 getDisplayMedia; no mobile equivalent), and mobile explicitly requests dominant-speaker and network-quality data it never renders (TwilioVideoRoom.tsx:716-717). Flagged so a literal-minded parity pass does not delete pre-join, the stage layout, the participants panel or retryable chat.

Not a web regression: absent from both repos, so parity already holds. Confirmed by name in the mobile repo — no flipCamera anywhere, no raise-hand/RSVP/recording/waiting-room/promote-to-host, no LIVE branch in HomeNotifications.tsx:266-308 (so web's routing.ts:41-85 omission is parity), and no AppState listener in the Twilio room. The doc itself marks these 'both'; carried here only so no row vanishes.

Capability is identical — enlarge one participant — and the container differs. Mobile's 'fullscreen' is an in-app expanded renderer inside the same chrome (TwilioVideoRoom.tsx:381-420), not an OS fullscreen. I also disproved the doc's escalation: it claims no way to enlarge a tile below md, but toggleLayout is unconditional (LiveRoom.tsx:372-374) and is offered in the options sheet at phone widths (LiveSheets.tsx:144-155); useViewportDefaults only chooses a default. Web keeps the filmstrip visible, which is the 'extra screen space used differently' case the brief calls wanted.

Layout and navigation restructuring, explicitly excluded. Nothing in the room becomes unreachable. The sharpest sub-claim — PushBridge toasting over a call — is not a mobile capability either: mobile calls displayNotification for chat and live pushes with no in-room suppression (push-notification.provider.tsx:440-460). If someone still wants an immersive room later, it is a layout change, not parity work.

Both platforms offer the same two destinations from a live group; only the container and click count differ. Mobile's sheet is itself gated on a live event existing (GroupsList.tsx:87-101), so once live-badge-truth lands, web's header button covers the same cases. The real defect underneath this row — a Join live button that appears when nothing is live — is captured as a sub_item of live-badge-truth.

Discoverability, not capability. The hide control (the Active checkbox) is always present on web and fetchLiveSessions already selects `active`, so hiding a session works and the Hidden tab appears the moment one exists. No mobile capability is unavailable to a web host.

toggleSpeaker is defined and returned but has zero call sites in the mobile repo — grep over ~/cancerbuddyapp/src finds only useTwilioRoom.ts:460 and :519. Porting a speakerphone toggle would be porting a control no mobile user can press. Web's audio-output picker with setSinkId is the correct behaviour and already ships (RemoteAudio.tsx:54-61).

The fallback navigates to TabsNavigator.Live, which TabsNavigator.tsx:30-42 never mounts for any user type — so on mobile a live push with a missing eventId lands nowhere. Correct web behaviour (fall back to /groups/{groupId}) is folded into live-push-deep-link's acceptance test rather than reproduced.

Unreachable, and I confirmed the ternary the doc rests on: in TabsNavigator.tsx:30-42 the `route.name === TabsNav.Live` clause is OR-ed at the top level, outside the SUPPORT user-type condition, so the Live tab is null for every user. The screens behind it are stubs (VideoControls.tsx:37 messages with no setter, :42-44 empty send, :106 isSendDisabled={true}). The one salvageable idea — ad-hoc 'go live now' — is a product gap on both platforms and is recorded under live-both-platforms-absent, not as a web regression.

Architectural note, not a capability gap. The room does not consume the groups context at all (no useGroups() in components/live/**) and re-fetches its own session, so tearing the provider down on entry costs a user nothing. Mobile's provider does survive into the room but nothing there reads it either.

Two source comments, no user-facing behaviour. Worth deleting opportunistically while touching liveGroups.ts for live-calendar-visibility-and-status and manageLives.ts for manage-lives-freshness, so it needs no work item of its own.

notes:
ORDERING. live-badge-truth must land first — three other items read from it. live-session-entry-points is not merely convenience, it is a hard blocker created by fixing live-badge-truth: `inLive` is flipped server-side by the first join (lib/live/session.ts:70-82 says so in its own comment), and today every path into /live/[eventId] on web is gated on inLive already being true. So the moment the badge query is corrected, no web host can start a session at all. These two should ship as one PR or back-to-back. live-calendar-visibility-and-status touches lib/groups/liveGroups.ts + types.ts, which live-badge-truth does not, so it can run in parallel.

DOC ERRORS FOUND (the input doc was wrong in both directions):
1. Cross-screen #9 claims that below `md` there is no way to enlarge one participant. False — toggleLayout is unconditional (LiveRoom.tsx:372-374) and appears in the options sheet at phone widths (LiveSheets.tsx:144-155). useViewportDefaults supplies a default only.
2. §4 row 6 ("sensible back-target after deep link") is listed as ❌ missing; web already derives backHref from the session's groupId (LiveRoom.tsx:126).
3. The doc's headline count of "18 ❌ and 12 ⚠️ true web-vs-mobile gaps" over-counts. After verification there are 6 buildable GAP items covering 26 doc rows; the rest are presentation, both-platforms-absent, mobile dead code, or web-ahead.
4. The doc does NOT surface the start-a-session blocker described above, which is the most consequential thing in this area.

OVERLAPS WITH OTHER PARITY DOCS:
- live-schedule-guardrails and manage-lives-freshness live in components/profile/ManageLivesScreen.tsx + lib/profile/manageLives.ts. docs/parity/profile.md owns that screen's form details and will very likely list the same four guard rails and the same refresh/timestamp rows. Merge them there or here, not both. The lifecycle framing (§5, cross-screen #7) is why they are here.
- live-push-deep-link touches public/firebase-messaging-sw.js, lib/push/pushClient.ts and components/push/PushBridge.tsx, which docs/parity/updates-notifications.md and docs/PUSH.md also cover. docs/PUSH.md:249 records "route everything else to /groups" as intentional; that decision predates /live/[eventId] and this item overturns it — update PUSH.md in the same change.
- live-badge-truth touches lib/groups/GroupsProvider.tsx and lib/groups/groupQueries.ts, shared with docs/parity/groups-feeds.md. The GroupFeed "Join live" button and the GroupsSidebar live/rest split are consumers, not separate items.

SHARED-LAYER CAVEAT: none of these six need media-upload, rich-text, modals, age-rules or unsaved-guard. Push is not one of the named layers, so live-push-deep-link is marked `none`; if a push-routing layer is created during the merge, that item belongs to it. live-badge-truth and live-groups-provider-scope are marked `realtime` because they sit on the existing AppSync onCreateLiveStreamingGroupCustom subscription, which itself needs no work.

UNRESOLVED QUESTION for the product owner (not a build item): should /groups/calendar link every upcoming row into the room the way mobile does, or only rows within some window of their start time? Mobile lets anyone walk in at any time and relies on the token Lambda to refuse; web's current gating was a deliberate improvement (docs/LIVE.md:160). live-session-entry-points needs at minimum the host's own session to be reachable pre-live; whether that extends to all members is a decision, and the acceptance test above assumes the mobile behaviour.

items.title: Enrollment and login analytics parity (bmcf_enrollment + first-action flags)
items.capability: Web-originated registrations and logins appear in the product funnel and first-action metrics, so the web app is not invisible to the same measurement mobile has.
sub_items: Emit the bmcf_enrollment event at the end of finalizeUserEnrollment (mobile emits it from LoadingPersonalInformation)

Set the 5 first-action flags (chatWithFirstBuddy, connectWithFirstBuddy, joinFirstGroup, comment, post) to 'true' on every successful login, as mobile's Login.tsx does — web only seeds them to 'false' at enrollment finalize, and nothing on web ever reads them
items.acceptance: Unit test with the analytics emitter injected/mocked: finalizeUserEnrollment calls it once with event name 'bmcf_enrollment'; the login success handler sets all 5 storage keys to 'true'. Both are pure-ish call-site assertions, no human needed. Note the emitter itself does not exist yet — see the ordering note.
items.evidence: WEB has no analytics provider at all: `grep -rn 'logEvent|gtag|firebase/analytics' lib components app` returns nothing and there is no lib/analytics directory; lib/user-signup/userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:90-96 declares ENROLLMENT_ANALYTICS_KEYS and seeds them to 'false', and `grep -rn 'chatWithFirstBuddy' lib components app` shows no reader. MOBILE src/screens/signIn/Login/Login.tsx:41-57 writes all five to 'true' on login; LoadingPersonalInformation.tsx:142 emits bmcf_enrollment.

demotions.why: Doc rows for the Welcome/splash screen, 'No'→Sign in, 'Yes'→Sign up and the 'Powered by' BMCF logo are all marked ✅ in the doc and confirmed on web at app/(auth)/page.tsx + app/(auth)/WelcomeSplash.tsx with sign-in/register links in the nav and MobileMenu.tsx. No work.

Mobile's literal 'Welcome! / Are you new here?' wording replaced by landing.heroHeading marketing copy, and mobile's Animated.parallel/sequence entrance replaced by hero-fade-up/hero-fade-in CSS keyframes. Same two destinations reachable; copy and motion only.

Eleven ✅ login rows re-confirmed: heading (app/(auth)/login/page.tsx), email input with type=email/autoComplete/autoCapitalize=none, password input with eye toggle, blur-only errors (RHF mode onBlur) plus all-fields-on-submit, submit loader, no social sign-in on either platform, no biometric on either platform, post-login destination, and the two rows that are N/A on web (native autofill ref sync, KeyboardStickyView). Also confirms docs/signup-flow-plan.md:225's 'Google + Apple stubs' claim is stale — no such code exists.

Email-required, email-format and password-required message wording differs between mobile's 'This field is required.' / 'Please provide a valid email.' and web's translated equivalents (lib/validations.ts:6-15). Same fields, same block-on-invalid behaviour, same meaning. Only the password `.min(8)` divergence is a real capability loss and it is carried in login-short-password-and-resume-orientation.

Mobile auto-navigates to SignUp with a toast on UserNotConfirmedException; web renders NotConfirmedBanner inline at app/(auth)/login/page.tsx:97,385 linking to /register — same destination reachable, container differs. Mobile shows raw Cognito text for other errors; web maps NotAuthorized/UserNotFound/InvalidParameter to a friendlier message and falls through to the raw message otherwise (lib/errors/userFacingMessage.ts:22-26), so no error is swallowed.

The `intro` step (StepIntro.tsx, 3 highlight cards + Start CTA + time note) has no mobile counterpart. Web-only onboarding context; must survive the parity work. Listed as ⚠️ PARTIAL in the doc but nothing is missing.

Mobile renders three long policies inline with a 'Read All' modal and an always-enabled 'I've read & accept'; web shows summaries with 'Read all' links to real routes (app/(legal)/privacy, /terms, /child-safety exist) and gates Continue on an explicit accept-all checkbox. Web is stricter, not weaker, and the legal record is preserved: lib/user-signup/cognitoUserSignupService.ts:206-207 writes acceptTerms:true + termsTimestamp exactly as mobile's src/utils/enrollment/register.ts:87 does.

PrivacyTermsUnderAgeDetected is a pure interstitial — its component body is a single <Image source={BMCF_Survivor.png}/> (src/.../PrivacyTermsUnderAgeDetected.tsx:6-15) with the 'you are a minor / you will need adult supervision' text coming from the copy map. Web collapses it into the guardian step, whose own copy asks the parent/guardian to fill in the info. Mobile page collapsed into the next web screen; no capability.

PrivacyTermsUnderAge's four fields (guardianFullName, guardianEmail, consent checkbox, supervision checkbox) and the CREATE_GUARDIAN Lambda call all exist on web at StepGuardian.tsx + app/register/page.tsx:557. Doc already marks ✅.

Mobile's guardian-OTP resend calls resendConfirmationCode(guardianEmail) → Auth.resendSignUp on the guardian's email, which is not a Cognito user at all (src/.../PrivacyTermsGuardianOTP.tsx:1,40-42) — it cannot deliver a new guardian code. Web's approach (re-invoke CREATE_GUARDIAN, stash the new id, verify against getGuardian(newId).code — app/register/page.tsx:628-657) is the behaviour that actually works. Keep web's.

Web's OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SEC = 30 (lib/signup/constants.ts:16) vs mobile's RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS = 60000 (src/utils/resendCooldown.ts:6) for all three OTPs. Web is more permissive — no mobile capability is lost. Flagged in notes as a rate-limit hardening ticket, not a parity gap.

The doc claims web lacks the 'Pick up where you left off / Create new account' bottom sheet and has 'no start-over escape hatch'. Both halves of the capability exist: the resume path is StartUserSignupResult RESUME_UNCONFIRMED surfaced as register.emailOtp.resumeHint (app/register/page.tsx:685, StepEmailOtp.tsx:43,91-96), and the escape hatch is the 'Change email' control (StepEmailOtp.tsx:128-132 → page.tsx:1073-1077 clears the session password, drops the resume info and returns to `credentials`, where a different email creates a new account). Only the sheet container differs.

Covers: auto-submit on the 6th digit vs an explicit Verify button (email/phone/guardian OTP), email masking on the OTP step (web-side privacy nicety), phone entry + phone OTP merged into one web screen with in-place reveal instead of two native stack screens, and 'Change number' being implicit (StepPhone.tsx:118 resets the OTP block when the number is edited) rather than a labelled control. Every action mobile offers is reachable; only containers and affordance labels differ. Phone validation message wording likewise (mobile has one format string, including its own typo 'shoud').

Doc error. The 'caregiver-only Patient minimum/maximum age inputs that mobile renders' are gated on `userType === CAREGIVER && onFilter` (PatientDiagnosisLayout.tsx:203), and the enrollment caller does not pass onFilter (ProfileSetupPatientDiagnosis.tsx:66-71 passes only formik/userType/userBirth/onValidRules). Those inputs belong to the buddies Filter screen (Filter.tsx:163), not registration — parity holds here; any gap belongs to buddies.md.

Three rows about Continue being enabled on web where mobile disables it: cgPatientAge (StepCGPatientAge.tsx renders Continue with no disabled prop plus a Skip link), profilePic (StepProfilePic.tsx:71 disabled only while uploading) and photos (StepPhotos.tsx:230 same). Mobile itself offers 'Maybe later' on profilePic and photos, so the same skip outcome is reachable on both; only cgPatientAge is genuinely stricter on mobile, and web being more permissive removes no mobile capability. Raised in notes as a product decision on data completeness, not a parity gap.

Four rows: ORDER_PRONOUNS_COPY, ORDER_RELATIONSHIPS_COPY, ORDER_LANGUAGES_COPY and ORDER_COPING_WITH_LOSS_COPY replaced by plain alphabetical sorts on web (app/register/_components/picker.tsx:9 sortAlpha, used by StepCGRelationship, StepAbout, StepLanguages, StepDiagnosis, StepMedicalCenter; `grep -rn ORDER_ lib app components` returns nothing). The brief explicitly excludes ordering from being a gap. Same options, same required-ness, same AppSync sources.

Mobile distinguishes ZIPCODE_NOT_FOUND from NETWORK_ERROR_COPY; web shows register.address.zipNotFound in both branches (StepAddress.tsx:76 and the catch at :94-95). Same block-on-error behaviour, different diagnosis text. Cosmetic error copy, noted for a follow-up polish; the zip→city→state cascade itself is ✅ per the doc and confirmed.

Two rows (the profilePic `otherDescription` swap and the generic `updateCopy` chrome row). Mobile swaps the title/description to 'Nice choice! To confirm your profile picture, tap continue.' after a photo is picked; web keeps one heading. Pure copy state, no capability — the photo can still be confirmed, replaced or removed via PhotoPicker/PhotoCropper.

Bio limit: mobile's input says maxLength 1000 while BioSchema enforces .max(300) — an internal contradiction, so mobile rejects text its own field invited. Web's coherent 1000 (matching the visible hint) is the correct behaviour; do not port 300. Related row: web shows the college sub-block when age is null while mobile renders nothing without a birth date — unreachable on web in practice because /register always collects birth before `about`, and showing more is not a lost capability.

Both 'Find buddies' and 'Explore groups' push /dashboard on web (StepAllSet.tsx:13); on mobile both CTAs also run the identical redirection() to home, so the only difference is which existing route is the landing page (app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx exists). Navigation only. pendingSupportChannel is handled earlier inside finalizeUserEnrollment, which the doc itself marks ✅.

Doc error (cross-screen gap #19). userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:246 filters `v !== null && v !== undefined && v !== ""` — strict comparison, so boolean `false` survives, and :213/:215 explicitly set `cancerloss: values.cancerloss || false` and `CurrentlyInCollege: values.isUniversityStudent || false`. An intentionally-false value IS written to UPDATE_USER, exactly as mobile does.

Doc error (cross-screen gap #26). Mobile's constant is named CREATE_SUPPORT_ORGANIZATIONS_USER but its body is `mutation createSupportOrgUser($input: CreateSupportOrgUserInput!)` (src/graphql/mutations/user.ts:225-227) — byte-identical operation and input type to web's CREATE_SUPPORT_ORG_USER (userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:62-66). Same resolver; nothing to confirm.

USER_REGISTER_STEPS lists only 6 of the 22 steps (lib/user-signup/constants.ts:54-61), so RegisterShell.tsx:88-94 computes stepIndex 0 and an empty heading for the 15 post-phone steps while mobile shows real progress on every screen. A progress indicator is visual chrome, which the brief excludes. Genuine defect worth a standalone ticket — flagged in notes — but not a capability gap.

Mobile drives titles/descriptions from ENROLLMENT_DEFAULT_COPIES(name) with {name} interpolation on every screen; web uses per-step i18n keys and interpolates the first name on only a few. Copy carrying the same meaning.

Four ✅ chrome rows confirmed: the HELP affordance with the same three categories submitting via USERS_LAMBDA (components/auth/HelpDialog.tsx in RegisterShell), swipe-back-disabled being N/A on web (the URL watermark governs), the back button on OTP screens, and in-memory-only draft storage with no localStorage (lib/user-signup/storage.ts).

Doc error (chrome row 'Resume for a half-finished account' and cross-screen gap #15). The claim is that quitting at `about` gets you classified DONE and dropped into /groups. It cannot: classifyRow requires BOTH a verified phone and a non-empty userType (lib/login/cognitoLoginService.ts:80-86), and userType is only ever written by the final UPDATE_USER at the loading step (userEnrollmentFinalize.ts:206) — mobile is identical (LoadingPersonalInformation.tsx:57,124 via UpdateRegisterUserUtil). So a user who quits at `about` has no userType and is classified RESUME_USER_ROLE, re-entering the wizard at `userRole` and walking forward. Mobile's unrolledPath restarts them at PrivacyTermsContract (EnrollmentProvider.utils.tsx:35-43), i.e. earlier. Both platforms lose the in-memory draft.

clampToReachableUserStep in lib/navigation/userStepGate.ts (with USER_FLOW_ORDER at :20-45) is forward-only URL-tamper hardening with no mobile counterpart. Must survive the caregiver-routing change in register-caregiver-medical-steps — that item adds steps to the reachable path, so the watermark's ordering must stay consistent.

Mobile's single name field runs validateName (REGEX_VALIDATE_NAME/REGEX_VALIDATE_EMOJIS) plus haveLastName; web's two fields (lib/signup/validation.ts:29-37, trim + min 1 + max 60 each) already enforce first-and-last-name structurally, so only the emoji/character-class *rejection* is absent. That makes web more permissive, not less capable — no mobile capability is lost. Raised in notes as a display-name hygiene product decision.

Two rows. (a) Masked mm/yyyy free-text vs MonthYearPicker's two selects — an input-affordance change that makes most of mobile's messages unreachable (a picker cannot emit month 13). (b) The age ceiling: mobile MAXIMUM_AGE = 130 (src/utils/birth.ts:72), web MAX_AGE = 120 (lib/signup/constants.ts:5). The divergence only affects birth years implying age 121–130 — no living person — and web's 120 is internally consistent with its own MIN_BIRTH_YEAR. Immaterial; keep 120.

Mobile attaches an InputHint tooltip ('Why do we ask this? Your age qualifies you to use this app and helps find buddies close to your age.') to the birth field on PrivacyTermsIntroduction and CGPatientAge; web's StepProfile.tsx:91-98 shows only a formatted 'born' confirmation hint. A rationale tooltip conveys no capability — the field is completed identically either way.

Nine of the fifteen Step-3 field-delta rows are pure message-wording differences over identical rules: email required, email format (Yup .email() vs the strict regex at lib/signup/validation.ts:66 — both reject the same practical mistakes), password >=8, >=1 digit, >=1 uppercase, confirm required, confirm must match, already-registered-and-confirmed wording, plus the static bullet hint vs the live meter. The lowercase and special-character rows are marked ✅ (same [!?¿@#$%^&*_] class), and the unconfirmed-email row is ✅ via RESUME_UNCONFIRMED. Only the meter's missing special-char check is real and is carried in password-meter-missing-special-char-rule.

Mobile toasts ALERT_CODE_RECENTLY_SENT ('A code was already sent recently…'); web conveys the same state structurally by disabling the resend control behind a visible countdown (OTP_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SEC, app/register/page.tsx:648 setGuardianResendLeft and siblings). The information reaches the user either way.

The doc says LimitExceededException 'falls through to the generic Something went wrong'. It does not: lib/errors/userFacingMessage.ts:22-26 returns `err.message` when present, so Cognito's own 'Attempt limit exceeded, please try after some time.' surfaces at every call site that uses userFacingErrorMessage (e.g. app/register/page.tsx:620,650). Mobile's ALERT_TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS is friendlier phrasing of the same information — copy quality, not a missing capability.

EXISTING_EMAIL_WRONG_PASSWORD (lib/user-signup/cognitoUserSignupService.ts) plus the phone ALREADY_IN_USE handling (:379, surfaced at app/register/page.tsx:812) and the retry button on the loading step have no mobile counterpart — mobile just fails. Must survive the parity pass.

Five rows — REQUIRED_UPDATE screen, OPCIONAL_UPDATE screen, the useUpdate/UpdateStorage nag throttle (0th and 3rd backgrounding), react-native-check-version needsUpdate, and the 'Update assistant' UpdateModal. All are app-store binary-version mechanics: they exist because a phone can be pinned to an old build. A browser loads the current deploy on every navigation, so there is no version a web member can be stuck on and no mobile capability they lack. Not strictly a container swap, but not a gap either — filing under PRESENTATION rather than inventing a bucket. The one adjacent web-native idea (a 'new build available, reload' prompt for a long-lived tab) is optional polish, not parity; see notes. The maintenance half of the subsystem IS carried, in app-status-maintenance-gate.

Four rows: the cancerbuddy:// custom-scheme prefix (no browser analogue), the cold-start getInitialURL queue with pendingDeepLinkUrl / lastConsumedUrl de-duping and the 800 ms delayed navigation, and the linking.subscribe background variant. These exist to work around React Navigation mounting a deep link as the initial route with nothing behind it (linking.js:5-8,32-41); a browser URL is the initial route by construction. Native navigation plumbing, no capability. The destination those URLs need is carried in deeplink-buddyid-landing.

Two rows. In-app Buddy-ID entry exists on web with the full guard set — components/buddies/BuddyIdSheet.tsx:53-70 checks not-found, self, isSnooze and connectAgeRulesBuddySearching, matching mobile's useValidateRules; components/profile/BuddyIdScreen.tsx also accepts a pasted link and strips the prefix (:93). The DeepLink sub-screens (DeepUserGallery, DeepJournalList, DeepJournalEntryDetail, Profile) all exist under app/(app)/buddies/[userId]/**. Camera QR scanning is deliberately not offered on web (documented at BuddyIdScreen.tsx:9-12) because typing a short id covers the same lookup — an input-method difference.

Three ✅ rows confirmed: Amplify default browser storage deliberately not cookieStorage (the documented HTTP 431 cause), silent session-expiry redirect, and pendingSupportChannel handled inside finalizeUserEnrollment.

Three rows about auth architecture, not capability. (a) Mobile hydrates one AuthenticatedUser blob in AuthProvider.restoreUser(); web re-checks per protected subtree via AuthGuard → hasValidSession (components/auth/AuthGuard.tsx:36-49, lib/auth-client.ts:20-28) and has a cached wide user read for the profile subtree (lib/profile/ProfileProvider.tsx). (b) Mobile's 60-minute setInterval refresh is unnecessary because Auth.currentSession() refreshes with the refresh token on every check. (c) On refresh failure web redirects to '/' without clearing the stale Amplify cache — worth a small hardening ticket (noted) but the user-visible outcome, being signed out and returned to the entry page, is identical.

The doc's '❌ MISSING — sign-out does almost nothing' (also cross-screen gap #5) is refuted at HEAD: components/app-shell/AccountSheet.tsx:62-72 runs unregisterPushDevice() → disconnectStream() → signOut() in mobile's order, with the ordering rationale documented in-code. Mobile's remaining steps are no-ops for web: the LOGOUT lambda and the UserDeviceToken row deletion both concern a device-token row web never writes (see login-users-lambda-bootstrap). Two narrow residuals belong to updates-notifications.md, not here: unregisterPushDevice early-returns when currentToken is null, and web lacks mobile's 4 s runSafely per-step timeout (src/context/auth/useAuth.ts:249-260).

proxy.ts:32 leaves PROTECTED_PREFIXES empty and :56-58 getSessionFromCookie always returns false, so gating is client-side via AuthGuard — a documented tradeoff forced by keeping Cognito tokens out of cookies. Mobile has no server-side route protection to be at parity with, so no mobile capability is missing. Belongs to docs/SECURITY.md Phase B/C, not to this parity programme.

UserRecoveryCodeVerification, UserRecoveryLoginWithoutEmail and UserRecoveryPassword (enrollmentPath indices 6-8) have no mapping in redirection.ts or conditions.ts that lands a counter on 6, 7 or 8 — they exist only as offset padding (userRecoveryGroup.length + N, e.g. conditions.ts:70). Their real purpose, resuming an unconfirmed signup, is covered on web by RESUME_UNCONFIRMED.

PrivacyTermsAlertChild (index 4, 'You need to be 8 years old…') is unreachable: verified at src/utils/enrollment/conditions.ts:76-82, RedirectVerificationConditionUtil returns 1 for the 8-12 branch AND 1 for the <=7 branch in both the mail and non-mail paths, so the counter never lands on index 4 — under-8 users enter the guardian flow on mobile too. Consequently neither platform has a minimum-age floor, and web's declared-but-unread CHILD_MIN_AGE / GUARDIAN_MAX_BIRTH_YEAR (lib/signup/constants.ts:3,8) plus the unused PRONOUN_OPTIONS/PRONOUN_LABELS (:19-33) are dead constants to delete, not a gap to close. Adding a floor would be a new product rule, not parity — see notes.
PersonalInfoNotification (enrollmentGroups/notifications/) is never imported into any screen group and hardcodes "Glad you're here, anna!". Unreachable.

Two mobile defects the doc lists so nobody ports them. (1) EnrollmentBackButton computes withoutButton then discards it through a literal `{true ? … : …}` (src/navigation/enrollment/EnrollmentBackButton.tsx:56), so the back arrow appears even on OTP screens. (2) RedirectBackVerificationConditionUtil compares `path.length < 32` (conditions.ts:34) while enrollmentPath.length is 28, so the check is always true and Back from AccountSetupUserRole/AccountSetupPhoneNumber throws a brand-new user all the way to PrivacyTermsContract. Web's forward-only watermark plus per-step back targets is the correct behaviour; do not reproduce either.

Cross-screen gaps #16 and #17's documentation half: docs/signup-flow-plan.md describes a 4-step /signup at app/(auth)/signup with a mock service, localStorage drafts and Google/Apple stubs — none of which exists (the flow is 22 steps at /register backed by lib/user-signup/cognitoUserSignupService.ts). Doc hygiene: rewrite or delete. The code half of #17 (deleting the lib/auth.ts and app/actions/auth.ts stubs) is carried as a sub_item of auth-password-reset-flow.

notes:
ORDERING / DEPENDENCIES
1. `auth-password-reset-flow` and `register-caregiver-medical-steps` are independent of every other item and of each other (different directories: app/(auth)+lib/login vs app/register). Start both; they parallelize cleanly.
2. `register-caregiver-medical-steps` must land before or with any change to lib/navigation/userStepGate.ts, because it lengthens the caregiver's reachable path and the forward-only watermark (see demotion register-step-watermark-web-only) derives from USER_FLOW_ORDER.
3. `register-login-analytics-events` is BLOCKED: web has no analytics provider at all (no lib/analytics, no logEvent/gtag/firebase-analytics import anywhere). It cannot ship until cross-cutting.md's analytics layer exists. Do not start it standalone — it would be an emitter with nothing behind it. Its acceptance test is written against an injected emitter so it can be authored now and wired later.
4. `login-users-lambda-bootstrap` is shippable now, but the `token` field of the payload is blocked on backend work owned by updates-notifications.md finding 11 (UserDeviceToken has no platform/provider column, and the web Firebase project cancerbuddy-web-73c0d differs from the sender's cancerbuddy-demo). Land the invocation with token omitted; do not wait.
5. `password-meter-missing-special-char-rule`, `register-verified-phone-echo`, `login-short-password-and-resume-orientation` are all xs and touch three different files — batch them into one housekeeping PR.

OVERLAPS WITH OTHER AREA DOCS (merge step must dedupe)
- `deeplink-buddyid-landing` overlaps buddies.md / PARITY.md finding 7. The BuddyIdScreen.tsx:88-104 missing self/snooze/age guards appear in both docs. PARITY.md's fix also gates components/buddies/BuddyProfileScreen.tsx:447-481 and adds a server-side assertion before CREATE_CONNECTION — those belong to buddies.md, not here. Implement the guard ONCE as a shared function and let both items consume it.
- `login-users-lambda-bootstrap` overlaps updates-notifications.md finding 11 (device-token registration) and cross-cutting.md (lambda verbs). The FCM-dedupe row from this doc's session table is folded into it as a note-only sub_item.
- `register-login-analytics-events` overlaps cross-cutting.md's analytics inventory. This doc contributes exactly two events (bmcf_enrollment, the 5 login flags); everything else is cross-cutting's.
- `app-status-maintenance-gate` is a new cross-cutting layer (`app-status`) that nothing else in this doc needs, but a maintenance gate wraps the whole authenticated shell — check cross-cutting.md before choosing the mount point (app/(app)/layout.tsx vs the root layout, since /register and /login should also be gated).

CORRECTIONS OWED TO THE SOURCE DOC (it is wrong in both directions; fix when touching the code)
- Line 214 and cross-screen gap #15 ("web cannot resume mid-profile; quit at `about` and you are classified DONE and dropped into /groups") are FALSE. userType is only written at the final UPDATE_USER on both platforms, so classifyRow returns RESUME_USER_ROLE. Web resumes at `userRole`; mobile restarts at PrivacyTermsContract.
- Cross-screen gap #19 ("finalizeUserEnrollment strips falsy values, so cancerloss:false is never written") is FALSE. The filter is `v !== null && v !== undefined && v !== ""` — strict, so `false` survives.
- Cross-screen gap #26 (support-org mutation name differs) is FALSE. Mobile's CREATE_SUPPORT_ORGANIZATIONS_USER constant contains the identical `createSupportOrgUser` operation.
- Cross-screen gap #23 ("LimitExceeded collapses into Something went wrong") is FALSE. userFacingErrorMessage returns err.message, so Cognito's own rate-limit text surfaces.
- Cross-screen gap #5 (sign-out does almost nothing) is refuted at HEAD — AccountSheet.tsx:62-72 already does the push/Stream teardown.
- Cross-screen gap #6 ("returning users never re-run the GetStream/Users LOGIN lambdas") is half wrong: the GetStream half runs lazily at lib/chat/streamToken.ts:52. Only the USERS_LAMBDA half is missing.
- Line 191's "web also drops the caregiver-only Patient minimum/maximum age inputs" is out of scope — those are gated on `onFilter`, which enrollment never passes; they belong to the buddies Filter screen.
- Lines 283 and 316-321 assert that the shared bonemarrow.org Buddy-ID URL "resolves to app/not-found.tsx" on this app. It does not: that host is 35.185.44.232, separate from cancerbuddy.com, and serves both .well-known files (resolved in PARITY.md Q2). `deeplink-buddyid-landing` is therefore scoped to making /buddyId/<id> work on THIS app's domain, not to rescuing mobile deep links, which are healthy.

REAL DEFECTS I DEMOTED (not capability gaps, but file them so they are not lost)
- Progress bar reports "step 1 of 6" and an empty heading for 15 of the 22 register steps (USER_REGISTER_STEPS covers only the Phase-1 six). Visual chrome by the brief's rules, but plainly broken. xs fix: extend USER_REGISTER_STEPS to the full flow or derive from USER_FLOW_ORDER.
- OTP resend cooldown is 30 s on web vs 60 s on mobile for all three OTPs. Web is more permissive, so not a gap, but Cognito's own rate limiter will start rejecting; align to 60 s.
- AuthGuard redirects on a failed session check without clearing the stale Amplify token cache, so the invalid tokens stay in localStorage.
- cgPatientAge is skippable on web and mandatory on mobile — a product decision on caregiver data completeness, worth asking the owner alongside register-caregiver-medical-steps since both concern the same missing caregiver data.
- Web accepts emoji and arbitrary characters in firstName/lastName where mobile rejects them. Display-name hygiene product decision.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- What does the USERS_LAMBDA `login` verb actually provision beyond device-token registration? Neither repo contains the Lambda. If the answer is "nothing else", `login-users-lambda-bootstrap` collapses into the push backlog and can be dropped. Ask the backend owner before building.
- Neither platform enforces a minimum age (mobile's under-8 screen is unreachable, web's CHILD_MIN_AGE is unread), so a birth year implying age 3 passes and enters the guardian flow on both. That is a live child-safety/COPPA question, but closing it is a NEW product rule, not parity work — escalate rather than silently porting mobile's dead intent.

items.title: Feed media upload layer + post/comment attachment tray
items.capability: A mobile user can attach images, videos and PDFs to a group post or a comment; a web user cannot attach anything at all.
sub_items: post-media-tray: attachment tray for the composer (1 item = hero card capped 190px; 1 PDF = file row with `PDF · size`; 2+ = 104px thumb strip with dashed Add tile; video = paused first frame + duration pill; tap = full-screen preview)
media-preview-strip: 72px pending-media thumbnails with a circular X remove badge, play overlay on video

utils/feedMedia.ts: the S3 upload path for feed media (feed posts have no Stream CDN) persisting `{type,bucket,region,key,mime,w,h,duration,name,size}`, presigned `expires:900`, cached 14 min, `extFromMime` quicktime→mov
ChatAttachmentMenu 'Add to post' / 'Add to comment' entry points (NewPostScreen.tsx:246, groups NewPost.tsx:102, both PostDetails)
msg-send paperclip on the post-comment composer — web's comment box is a bare textarea with no attach affordance
photo/useChatMediaPicker document rules: PDFs only, MAX_DOCUMENT_SIZE_MB = 20, UUID filename rewrite
platform-capabilities row 'Video playback ❌ — not built for feed/chat attachments' (create side)
items.acceptance: Playwright: on /groups/<id>, `setInputFiles` a jpg + a pdf into the composer, submit, and assert (a) at least one PUT to the S3 bucket host was issued, and (b) the Stream `addActivity` request body contains `attachments[0].key`, `.mime`, `.size`. Plus a unit test on the new `buildFeedAttachment(file)` asserting the exact 9-key shape and `extFromMime('video/quicktime') === 'mov'`.
items.evidence: Web `createPost` accepts `attachments?: unknown[]` (lib/groups/posts.ts:293) but no caller ever supplies one — PostComposer.tsx has no file input at all (only a textarea, :56-72) and PostThread's comment box is a raw `<textarea>` (:266). OPEN QUESTIONS NEEDING A HUMAN DECISION (do not guess):
- age-and-limit-constant-alignment includes letting under-8s register (mobile has no minimum age at all, only a guardian branch). Web's CHILD_MIN_AGE = 8 may be a deliberate COPPA choice. Needs product sign-off; the MAX_AGE 120→130 and bio 300/1000 halves are safe to ship immediately.
- web lets a HOST browse buddies; mobile's userTypeAllowed maps HOST → []. Confirm which is intended before anyone "fixes" it.
- chat file allow-list: web accepts doc/docx/txt, mobile PDFs only. Pick one before adding the 20 MB cap.
- support-real-submission needs the /support infra decision (unauth identity-pool invoke rights vs an app/api route) and a product call on the ticket-id promise and the attachment picker.
- `newGetReactionsByPost`: web reads comments straight from Stream REST. Confirm with backend whether the Lambda path is required (e.g. for enrichment) before adding the verb.
